---
title: "Hand History Review"
date: "Generated `r format(Sys.Date(), '%b %d, %Y')`"
output:
  html_document:
    theme: flatly
    toc: true
    toc_float: true
    css: dashboard.css
params:
  hands_csv: "coinpoker_features.csv"
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 10, fig.height = 4.2, dpi = 110)
library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(ggplot2); library(scales); library(plotly); library(stringr)

green <- "#1f4e79"; red <- "#a8432f"; ink <- "#2b3a42"; grid <- "#e6e9ec"
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), panel.grid.major = element_line(color = grid),
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14, color = ink),
        axis.title = element_text(color = "#6b7780"), legend.title = element_blank()))
tt <- function(x) paste0(ifelse(x < 0, "-", ""), "$", comma(abs(x), accuracy = 0.01))  # ₮ = USDT ~ $1

# Reusable "layered" bar chart: latest (green) over previous (grey), with the reg/ideal range as a
# distinct dashed-border band, plus a key. df needs: x, lab, prev, cur, and optional lo/hi (ideal).
layer_cols <- c("Latest" = green, "Previous" = "#c4ccd1", "Ideal range" = "#dbeafa")
layered_bars <- function(df, title, ylab = "%", w = 0.62) {
  has_band <- "lo" %in% names(df) && any(!is.na(df$lo))
  g <- ggplot(df)
  if (has_band)
    g <- g + geom_rect(aes(xmin = x - w/2 - 0.03, xmax = x + w/2 + 0.03, ymin = lo, ymax = hi, fill = "Ideal range"),
                       color = "#7fa8cf", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.45, alpha = 0.5)
  g + geom_col(aes(x = x, y = prev, fill = "Previous"), width = w) +
    geom_col(aes(x = x, y = cur, fill = "Latest"), width = w) +
    geom_text(aes(x = x, y = prev, label = sprintf("%.1f", prev)), vjust = -0.5, size = 2.7, color = "#7c868c") +
    geom_text(aes(x = x, y = pmax(cur - 0.6, 0.7), label = sprintf("%.1f", cur)), vjust = 1, size = 3.4,
              color = "white", fontface = "bold") +
    scale_fill_manual(name = NULL, values = layer_cols,
                      breaks = c("Latest", "Previous", "Ideal range"), drop = FALSE) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = df$x, labels = df$lab) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
    labs(title = title, x = NULL, y = ylab) + theme(legend.position = "top")
}

# Read the ENRICHED feature CSV (starting-hand class, fees, range model, postflop engine,
# leak/win tags all precomputed in features_coinpoker.R). Self-heal rebuilds it when it's
# missing, lacks any currently-required column, OR is STALER than the raw hands CSV (so a
# direct knit after re-parsing can't silently use old features).
fcsv <- params$hands_csv
raw_csv <- "coinpoker_hands.csv"
req_cols <- c("hand169", "range_dir", "in_open_range", "made_river",
              "river_bluff", "lk_loose_entry", "primary_leak", "win_source")
dec_csv <- "coinpoker_decisions.csv"
needs_build <- !file.exists(fcsv) ||
  !all(req_cols %in% names(read.csv(fcsv, nrows = 1))) ||
  !file.exists(dec_csv) || file.mtime(dec_csv) < file.mtime(fcsv) ||
  !("req_implied_x" %in% names(read.csv(dec_csv, nrows = 1))) ||
  (file.exists(raw_csv) && file.mtime(raw_csv) > file.mtime(fcsv))
if (needs_build) system2("Rscript", "features_coinpoker.R")
h <- read.csv(fcsv, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
dec <- read.csv(dec_csv, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)   # per-decision value attribution (Tier 1)
h$dt <- as.POSIXct(h$dt)
h <- h %>% arrange(dt)

# Presentation-only factors (ordering); the heavy feature engineering now lives upstream.
pos_lv <- c("EP2", "EP", "UTG", "MP", "HJ", "CO", "BTN", "SB", "BB")
h$hero_pos <- factor(h$hero_pos, levels = pos_lv[pos_lv %in% h$hero_pos])
lv <- h %>% distinct(sb, bb) %>% arrange(bb, sb) %>% mutate(s = paste0(sb, "/", bb)) %>% pull(s)
h$stake <- factor(paste0(h$sb, "/", h$bb), levels = lv)
cash <- filter(h, !is_bomb)   # exclude bomb pots from skill stats (forced action, no preflop)

bb100   <- function(d) sum(d$net_bb) / nrow(d) * 100
n_hands <- nrow(h); tot_net <- sum(h$net)
tot_rake <- sum(h$hero_rake); tot_splash <- sum(h$hero_splash); tot_fees <- sum(h$fees)
date_lo <- min(as.Date(h$dt)); date_hi <- max(as.Date(h$dt))

# ---- card-review renderer (used by several sections) -----------------------
# Suit glyphs via HTML entities (dodges the <U+...> string-output bug).
suit_ent <- c(s = "&spades;", h = "&hearts;", d = "&diams;", c = "&clubs;")
suit_col <- c(s = "#2b3a42", h = "#a8432f", d = "#a8432f", c = "#2b3a42")
card_html <- function(card) {
  if (is.na(card) || card == "") return("")
  r <- substr(card, 1, 1); s <- substr(card, 2, 2)
  sprintf('<span class="card" style="color:%s">%s<span class="suit">%s</span></span>', suit_col[s], r, suit_ent[s])
}
cards_html <- function(str) {
  if (is.na(str) || str == "") return('<span class="muted">-</span>')
  paste(vapply(strsplit(trimws(str), " ")[[1]], card_html, character(1)), collapse = "")
}
street_act <- function(bet, call) {
  if (!is.na(bet) && bet > 0) sprintf('<span class="act-bet">bet %s</span>', tt(bet))
  else if (!is.na(call) && call > 0) sprintf('<span class="act-call">called %s</span>', tt(call))
  else '<span class="muted">checked / -</span>'
}
default_flag <- function(r) {
  if (r$river_call > 0 && !is.na(r$sd_cat) && r$sd_cat %in% c("One Pair", "High Card")) "paid off river with a weak hand"
  else if (r$turn_call > 0 && r$net < 0) "called the turn, lost"
  else if (is.na(r$sd_cat)) "big pot, no showdown" else "review"
}
render_review_cards <- function(df, flagger = default_flag) {
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(df))) {
    r <- df[i, ]
    flag <- flagger(r)
    lost_to <- if (!is.na(r$villain_cards)) paste0("lost to ", cards_html(r$villain_cards), " (", r$villain_cat, ")") else ""
    made <- if (!is.na(r$sd_cat)) paste0("you made ", r$sd_cat) else "no showdown"
    cat(sprintf('<div class="review-hand"><div class="rh-head">%s <span class="rh-meta">%s &middot; %s/%s</span> <span class="rh-net %s">%s</span></div><div class="rh-streets">',
                cards_html(r$hero_cards), as.character(r$hero_pos), r$sb, r$bb,
                if (r$net >= 0) "pos" else "neg", tt(r$net)))
    cat(sprintf('<div class="street"><div class="st-name">Flop</div><div class="st-cards">%s</div><div class="st-act">%s</div></div>',
                cards_html(r$flop), street_act(r$hero_flop_bet, r$flop_call)))
    cat(sprintf('<div class="street"><div class="st-name">Turn</div><div class="st-cards">%s</div><div class="st-act">%s</div></div>',
                cards_html(r$turn_card), street_act(r$hero_turn_bet, r$turn_call)))
    cat(sprintf('<div class="street"><div class="st-name">River</div><div class="st-cards">%s</div><div class="st-act">%s</div></div>',
                cards_html(r$river_card), street_act(r$hero_river_bet, r$river_call)))
    cat(sprintf('</div><div class="rh-foot">%s &middot; %s &middot; <b>%s</b></div></div>', made, lost_to, flag))
  }
}
```

<div class="kpi-row">
<div class="kpi"><div class="kpi-label">Hands</div><div class="kpi-value">`r comma(n_hands)`</div><div class="kpi-sub">`r format(date_lo, "%b %d")` – `r format(date_hi, "%b %d, %Y")`</div></div>
<div class="kpi"><div class="kpi-label">Net result</div><div class="kpi-value `r if (tot_net>=0) "pos" else "neg"`">`r tt(tot_net)`</div><div class="kpi-sub">across `r length(unique(h$bb))` stake levels</div></div>
<div class="kpi"><div class="kpi-label">Win rate</div><div class="kpi-value `r if (bb100(h)>=0) "pos" else "neg"`">`r sprintf("%+.1f", bb100(h))`</div><div class="kpi-sub">bb / 100 hands</div></div>
<div class="kpi"><div class="kpi-label">VPIP / PFR</div><div class="kpi-value">`r percent(mean(cash$vpip),1)` / `r percent(mean(cash$pfr),1)`</div><div class="kpi-sub">preflop entry / raise</div></div>
<div class="kpi"><div class="kpi-label">Fees paid</div><div class="kpi-value neg">`r tt(tot_fees)`</div><div class="kpi-sub">rake + splash, `r tt(tot_fees/n_hands)` / hand</div></div>
</div>

<p class="meta">Hero's view, parsed from CoinPoker text histories. "bb/100" normalizes each hand by its own
big blind, so mixed stakes are comparable. Bomb pots (`r sum(h$is_bomb)`) are excluded from preflop
skill stats (no normal preflop action).</p>

# Progress tracker

Where your game is **right now** and whether it's moving the right way. Each point is a **day of
play** (computed fresh from de-duplicated hands, so overlapping or multi-day uploads can't double-count).
Days under 50 hands are dropped as too noisy. The table compares your **latest day** to the
**previous day** against a winning 6-max reg's range.

```{r progress-calc}
snaps <- tryCatch(read.csv("coinpoker_snapshots.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE), error = function(e) NULL)
if (!is.null(snaps)) { snaps$date <- as.Date(snaps$date); snaps <- snaps[snaps$n >= 50, , drop = FALSE]
                       snaps <- snaps[order(snaps$date), ] }
has_snaps <- !is.null(snaps) && nrow(snaps) >= 2
if (has_snaps) {
  cur <- snaps[nrow(snaps), ]; prv <- snaps[nrow(snaps) - 1, ]
  bands <- list(vpip = c(22, 27), pfr = c(18, 22), threebet = c(7, 12), cbet = c(50, 65),
                fold_to_cbet = c(40, 55), af = c(2, 3.5), wtsd = c(24, 28))
  labs <- c(vpip = "VPIP %", pfr = "PFR %", threebet = "3-bet %", cbet = "C-bet %",
            fold_to_cbet = "Fold to c-bet %", af = "Postflop AF", wtsd = "WTSD %")
  bstatus <- function(v, b) if (v < b[1]) "below" else if (v > b[2]) "above" else "in band"
  bdist <- function(v, b) if (v < b[1]) b[1] - v else if (v > b[2]) v - b[2] else 0
  # warnings/focus use only the high-sample preflop stats (every hand) -- per-day postflop
  # rates (c-bet, fold-to-cbet, AF, WTSD) are too noisy on a single day to flag.
  stable <- c("vpip", "pfr", "threebet")
}
```

<p class="meta">`r if (has_snaps) sprintf("Latest day: %s (%d hands) vs previous: %s (%d hands).", format(cur$date, "%b %d"), cur$n, format(prv$date, "%b %d"), prv$n) else "Need two 50+ hand days for trends."`</p>

```{r trend-table, eval=has_snaps}
tr <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(bands), function(k) {
  b <- bands[[k]]; cv <- cur[[k]]; pv <- prv[[k]]; d <- cv - pv
  data.frame(Stat = labs[k], `Latest day` = cv, `Prev day` = pv, `Change` = sprintf("%+.1f", d),
             `Reg range` = paste0(b[1], "-", b[2]), `Status` = bstatus(cv, b), check.names = FALSE)
}))
knitr::kable(tr, align = "lrrrrl", row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r warnings, eval=has_snaps, results='asis'}
w <- character(0)
for (k in stable) {
  b <- bands[[k]]; cv <- cur[[k]]; pv <- prv[[k]]; st <- bstatus(cv, b)
  if (st != "in band")
    w <- c(w, sprintf("<b>%s</b> is %s the reg range (%.1f vs %d-%d)", labs[k], st, cv, b[1], b[2]))
  if (bdist(cv, b) > bdist(pv, b) + 1.5)
    w <- c(w, sprintf("<b>%s</b> drifted <span class='down'>away from target</span> (%.1f, was %.1f)", labs[k], cv, pv))
  if (bdist(pv, b) > 0 && bdist(cv, b) == 0)
    w <- c(w, sprintf("<b>%s</b> came back <span class='up'>into range</span> (%.1f) - keep it.", labs[k], cv))
}
if (length(w)) {
  cat('<div class="warn"><div class="warn-title">Watch &amp; wins (latest day)</div><ul>')
  for (x in unique(w)) cat(paste0("<li>", x, "</li>"))
  cat('</ul></div>')
} else cat('<div class="ok">All key tendencies are inside the reg range on your latest day. Solid.</div>')
```

```{r focus, eval=has_snaps, results='asis'}
ds <- sapply(stable, function(k) bdist(cur[[k]], bands[[k]]))
worst <- names(which.max(ds))
foc <- if (max(ds) > 0) {
  sprintf("Pull <b>%s</b> toward range - it's the furthest off (now %.1f, target %d-%d).",
          labs[worst], cur[[worst]], bands[[worst]][1], bands[[worst]][2])
} else {
  "Tendencies are dialed in - shift focus to postflop discipline: fold one pair / busted draws to big turn-river bets, and bet your IP spots instead of calling."
}
cat(paste0('<div class="focus"><div class="focus-title">Focus for the next ~3 days</div>', foc,
           '<div class="focus-sub">Re-checks automatically the next time new hands are parsed.</div></div>'))
```

### Latest day vs previous

**Key:** dark blue = your **latest day**, grey behind = the **previous day** (a blue bar shorter than the
grey cap means the stat came down), dashed blue band = the **ideal reg range**.

```{r trend-bars, eval=has_snaps, fig.height=3.4}
key <- c("vpip", "pfr", "threebet")
td <- data.frame(x = seq_along(key), lab = unname(labs[key]),
                 prev = as.numeric(prv[key]), cur = as.numeric(cur[key]),
                 lo = sapply(key, function(k) bands[[k]][1]), hi = sapply(key, function(k) bands[[k]][2]))
layered_bars(td, "VPIP / PFR / 3-bet: latest day vs previous, vs ideal range")
```

Below, the same three tendencies **plus bb/100 (your actual win rate)** across your sessions. Points
are spaced **evenly by session, not by calendar date** (the date is in the hover) - so a month-long
break doesn't stretch into a misleading flat line. VPIP / PFR / 3-bet read off the **left** axis;
**bb/100 rides the right axis** (its own scale, since a day's win rate swings far wider than a percent
stat). Heads-up: one-day bb/100 is noisy - read its *direction over several sessions*, not any single point.

```{r trend-line, eval=has_snaps}
sl <- snaps; sl$idx <- seq_len(nrow(sl)); sl$dlab <- format(sl$date, "%b %d")
c_vpip <- "#9aa7b0"; c_pfr <- green; c_3bet <- ink; c_bb <- "#b98a3e"   # bb/100 = amber, its own axis
line_series <- function(p, yv, nm, col, dash = "solid", axis = "y") {
  add_trace(p, y = yv, name = nm, yaxis = axis, type = "scatter", mode = "lines+markers",
            line = list(color = col, width = 2.2, dash = dash), marker = list(color = col, size = 6),
            text = sl$dlab, hovertemplate = paste0("%{text}<br>", nm, ": %{y:.1f}<extra></extra>"))
}
plot_ly(sl, x = ~idx, height = 360) %>%
  line_series(~vpip,     "VPIP %",  c_vpip) %>%
  line_series(~pfr,      "PFR %",   c_pfr) %>%
  line_series(~threebet, "3-bet %", c_3bet) %>%
  line_series(~bb100,    "bb/100",  c_bb, dash = "dot", axis = "y2") %>%
  layout(title = list(text = "Key tendencies by session (evenly spaced; date in hover)",
                      font = list(size = 15, color = ink), x = 0.02),
         xaxis = list(title = "", tickmode = "array", tickvals = sl$idx, ticktext = sl$dlab,
                      tickangle = -40, tickfont = list(size = 10)),
         yaxis  = list(title = "VPIP / PFR / 3-bet (%)", rangemode = "tozero", zeroline = FALSE),
         yaxis2 = list(title = "bb/100", overlaying = "y", side = "right", showgrid = FALSE,
                       zeroline = TRUE, zerolinecolor = "#c9ced3", zerolinewidth = 1),
         legend = list(orientation = "h", x = 0, y = 1.12),
         hovermode = "x unified", margin = list(r = 62, t = 54))
```

By position, did the tightening land everywhere or just a few seats? Same key, with rough positional
VPIP targets as the band (blinds defend wide, so their ideal is broad). Seats under 15 hands/day dropped.

```{r pos-trend, eval=has_snaps, fig.height=3.4}
vpip_ideal <- list(UTG = c(15, 20), MP = c(17, 22), HJ = c(18, 24), CO = c(23, 29),
                   BTN = c(40, 48), SB = c(28, 40), BB = c(30, 46), EP = c(14, 19), EP2 = c(13, 18))
dprev <- snaps$date[nrow(snaps) - 1]; dcur <- snaps$date[nrow(snaps)]
pv_pos <- cash %>% filter(as.Date(dt) == dprev) %>% group_by(hero_pos) %>% summarise(prev = mean(vpip) * 100, np = n(), .groups = "drop")
cv_pos <- cash %>% filter(as.Date(dt) == dcur) %>% group_by(hero_pos) %>% summarise(cur = mean(vpip) * 100, nc = n(), .groups = "drop")
pt <- full_join(pv_pos, cv_pos, by = "hero_pos") %>%
  filter(!is.na(hero_pos), coalesce(np, 0) >= 15, coalesce(nc, 0) >= 15)
pt$hero_pos <- factor(pt$hero_pos, levels = pos_lv[pos_lv %in% pt$hero_pos])
pt <- pt %>% arrange(hero_pos) %>% mutate(x = row_number(), lab = as.character(hero_pos),
         lo = sapply(lab, function(p) vpip_ideal[[p]][1]), hi = sapply(lab, function(p) vpip_ideal[[p]][2]))
layered_bars(pt, "VPIP by position: latest day vs previous, vs ideal", ylab = "VPIP %")
```

### Costliest hands from the latest day

The costliest hands from your most recent day — laid out street by street with the board and your
action, so you can replay the decision. The flag is a guess at the leak.

```{r sus-hands, eval=has_snaps, results='asis'}
last_day <- max(snaps$date)
render_review_cards(cash %>% filter(as.Date(dt) == last_day) %>% arrange(net) %>% head(5))
```

## Results by stake

The same stats split by stake, with bb/100 at each level.

```{r by-stake}
bs <- cash %>% group_by(Stake = stake) %>%
  summarise(Hands = n(), `Net` = tt(sum(net)), `bb/100` = sprintf("%+.1f", sum(net_bb)/n()*100),
            VPIP = percent(mean(vpip), 1), PFR = percent(mean(pfr), 1), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(bs, align = "lrrrrr")
```

```{r by-stake-chart, fig.height=3.6}
bsc <- cash %>% group_by(stake) %>% summarise(bb100 = sum(net_bb)/n()*100, hands = n(), .groups = "drop")
ggplot(bsc, aes(stake, bb100, fill = bb100 >= 0)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6) + geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = ink) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%+.1f (n=%d)", bb100, hands)), vjust = ifelse(bsc$bb100 >= 0, -0.4, 1.2), size = 3.4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = green, `FALSE` = red), guide = "none") +
  labs(title = "Win rate by stake (bb / 100 hands)", x = NULL, y = "bb/100")
```

## Results by table

A quirk worth exploiting: CoinPoker's `table_id` isn't a one-off seating, it's a **persistent lobby
identity**: a table name recurs across many sessions, and each one hosts exactly one stake (no
mixing). So **table-level** history needs no player profiling at all; it's a direct readout of
Hero's own results at a specific, revisitable table. Standalone + wired into every
render (`table_ecology.R`).

```{r te-load}
te <- tryCatch(read.csv("coinpoker_table_ecology.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE), error = function(e) NULL)
```

```{r te-table, eval=!is.null(te)}
tt2 <- te %>% transmute(Table = table_id, Stake = stake, Hands = n_hands, `Avg players` = avg_players,
  `Hero VPIP` = percent(hero_vpip, 1), `Avg pot (bb, postflop)` = avg_pot_bb,
  `Multiway rate` = percent(multiway_rate, 1), Net = tt(net), `bb/100` = sprintf("%+.1f", bb100))
knitr::kable(tt2, align = "lccccccrr", caption = sprintf("Every table with >=30 hands (%d of %d total tables)", nrow(te), length(unique(h$table_id))))
```

```{r te-note, results='asis', eval=!is.null(te)}
big <- te[which.max(te$n_hands), ]
cat(sprintf('<p class="meta">Table <b>%s</b> alone accounts for <b>%s of all hands</b> in this dashboard (%d of them) and has been a <b>%s bb/100</b> venue (%s) &mdash; the single biggest venue. The avg-players-seated column has the strongest (if still small-sample, n=%d tables) relationship with results here: fuller tables have tended to run worse for Hero. Treat the correlation numbers printed by <code>table_ecology.R</code> as a hypothesis to keep watching, not a proven seat-selection rule at this sample size &mdash; but the per-table ranking itself is a direct, actionable readout: these are specific, revisitable tables, not anonymous one-off seatings.</p>',
  big$table_id, percent(big$n_hands / sum(te$n_hands), 1), big$n_hands,
  sprintf("%+.1f", big$bb100), tt(big$net), nrow(te)))
```

```{r te-missing, results='asis', eval=is.null(te)}
cat('<p class="meta">No <code>coinpoker_table_ecology.csv</code> found &mdash; run <code>Rscript table_ecology.R</code> (render does this automatically).</p>')
```

## Bankroll over time (in big blinds)

Cumulative bb (stake-normalized), so a swing at 50NL doesn't dwarf the rest. The x-axis is **hands played**,
not calendar date, so breaks between sessions don't stretch into long flat lines. Drag to zoom.

```{r bankroll, fig.height=4}
cb <- h %>% arrange(dt) %>% mutate(idx = row_number(), cum = cumsum(net_bb),
            text = paste0("hand ", idx, "<br>", format(dt, "%b %d %H:%M"), "<br>", stake, "<br>cum: ", round(cum), " bb"))
plot_ly(cb, x = ~idx, y = ~cum, type = "scatter", mode = "lines", line = list(color = green, width = 1.5),
        hoverinfo = "text", text = ~text, height = 360) %>%
  layout(xaxis = list(title = "hands played", gridcolor = grid),
         yaxis = list(title = "cumulative bb", gridcolor = grid, zeroline = TRUE, zerolinecolor = ink),
         margin = list(t = 20)) %>%
  config(displaylogo = FALSE, modeBarButtonsToRemove = c("select2d", "lasso2d", "autoScale2d"))
```

## Luck ledger for the deepest drawdown

Every downswing raises the same question: cards, bad beats, or leaks? This splits the answer into
three honestly-scoped luck components plus a residual, instead of one vague "variance" verdict.
**Card luck** = raw equity of the hands you were dealt vs a random hand (no board, no villain read —
purely "were your cards better or worse than usual"), monetized off your own full-sample regression.
**All-in luck** = equity at clean all-ins with cards to come vs what you actually collected.
**River-card luck** = for hands that reached a heads-up showdown street-by-street (not all-in), equity
right before the river card fell vs the actual result — did that one card flip who was ahead. Whatever
is left over is the **residual**: your decisions plus variance the other three don't touch. Standalone
tool (`python3 luck_ledger.py`, ~2-3 min) — not run on every render; DATA_DICTIONARY §10 has
the exact formulas and caveats.

```{r ll-load}
ll <- tryCatch(read.csv("coinpoker_luck_ledger.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE), error = function(e) NULL)
ll_ok <- !is.null(ll) && "downswing" %in% ll$window
```

```{r ll-chart, eval=ll_ok, fig.height=4.2}
lab <- c(card_luck = "Card luck", allin_luck = "All-in luck", river_card_luck = "River-card luck",
         residual = "Residual\n(decisions + other)", actual_net = "Actual net")
ord <- names(lab)
w <- ll[ll$window == "downswing", ]
w <- w[match(ord, w$component), ]
n_hands <- w$n_hands[w$component == "actual_net"]

plot_ly(w, x = unname(lab[w$component]), y = ~dollars, type = "waterfall",
        measure = c("relative", "relative", "relative", "relative", "total"),
        text = ~tt(dollars), textposition = "outside",
        increasing = list(marker = list(color = green)),
        decreasing = list(marker = list(color = red)),
        totals = list(marker = list(color = ink)),
        connector = list(line = list(color = grid)), height = 380) %>%
  layout(title = list(text = sprintf("Downswing decomposition since Jun 18 (%d hands)", n_hands), font = list(size = 14)),
         yaxis = list(title = "$", gridcolor = grid, zeroline = TRUE, zerolinecolor = ink),
         xaxis = list(title = NULL), margin = list(t = 40)) %>%
  config(displaylogo = FALSE, modeBarButtonsToRemove = c("select2d", "lasso2d", "autoScale2d"))
```

```{r ll-note, results='asis', eval=ll_ok}
d <- setNames(w$dollars, w$component)
badbeat <- d["allin_luck"] + d["river_card_luck"]
share <- function(x) percent(abs(x) / sum(abs(d[c("card_luck","allin_luck","river_card_luck","residual")])), 1)
cat(sprintf('<p class="meta">Window result: <b>%s</b>. Card luck is %s (%s). All-in luck (%s) and river-card luck (%s) together come to <b>%s</b>, about %s of the total swing. The <b>residual is %s</b>, about %s: decisions plus everything the model can&rsquo;t see, not automatically leaks (the leak ledger below gives the named-leak view of the same money).</p>',
  tt(d["actual_net"]),
  tt(d["card_luck"]), ifelse(abs(d["card_luck"]) < 20, "close to an average mix of hands", "a real departure from an average mix"),
  tt(d["allin_luck"]), tt(d["river_card_luck"]), tt(badbeat), share(badbeat),
  tt(d["residual"]), share(d["residual"])))
```

```{r ll-missing, results='asis', eval=!ll_ok}
cat('<p class="meta">No <code>coinpoker_luck_ledger.csv</code> found (or no downswing-window rows) &mdash; run <code>python3 luck_ledger.py</code> from the repo root to generate it (~2-3 min).</p>')
```

## Downswing simulator and win-rate estimate

Three questions on the same per-hand results, each carrying its own honest uncertainty instead of
one point estimate. DATA_DICTIONARY §11 has the exact methods and caveats. Standalone + wired into
every render (`downswing_sim.R`, ~2s).

```{r ds-load}
dd_sum <- tryCatch(read.csv("coinpoker_downswing_sim.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE), error = function(e) NULL)
dd_boot <- tryCatch(read.csv("coinpoker_bootstrap_dd.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE), error = function(e) NULL)
wr_post <- tryCatch(read.csv("coinpoker_winrate_posterior.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE), error = function(e) NULL)
wr_post_rb <- tryCatch(read.csv("coinpoker_winrate_posterior_rakeback.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE), error = function(e) NULL)
ror <- tryCatch(read.csv("coinpoker_risk_of_ruin.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE), error = function(e) NULL)
ds_ok <- !is.null(dd_sum) && !is.null(dd_boot) && !is.null(wr_post) && !is.null(ror)
has_rb_posterior <- !is.null(wr_post_rb)
```

### 1. Worst drawdown against simulated careers

```{r ds-dd-chart, eval=ds_ok, fig.height=3.8}
plot_ly(dd_boot, x = ~sim_dd_bb, type = "histogram", height = 320,
        marker = list(color = "#c4ccd1", line = list(color = "white", width = 0.5))) %>%
  layout(title = list(text = sprintf("5,000 simulated careers, same length as yours (%s hands)", comma(dd_sum$n_hands)), font = list(size = 13)),
         xaxis = list(title = "worst peak-to-trough drawdown (bb)", gridcolor = grid),
         yaxis = list(title = "simulated careers", gridcolor = grid),
         shapes = list(list(type = "line", x0 = dd_sum$actual_dd_bb, x1 = dd_sum$actual_dd_bb,
                             y0 = 0, y1 = 1, yref = "paper", line = list(color = red, width = 2, dash = "dash"))),
         annotations = list(list(x = dd_sum$actual_dd_bb, y = 1, yref = "paper", yanchor = "bottom",
                                  showarrow = FALSE, text = "your actual worst swing", font = list(color = red, size = 11))),
         margin = list(t = 40)) %>%
  config(displaylogo = FALSE, modeBarButtonsToRemove = c("select2d", "lasso2d", "autoScale2d"))
```

```{r ds-dd-note, results='asis', eval=ds_ok}
cat(sprintf('<p class="meta">Your worst drawdown so far is <b>%.0f bb</b>. Resampling your own per-hand results (order scrambled, same total volume) %.0f%% of simulated careers hit a swing at least that bad %s the median simulated worst swing is %.0f bb. %s</p>',
  dd_sum$actual_dd_bb, 100 * dd_sum$percentile,
  ifelse(dd_sum$percentile > 0.3, "purely by chance &mdash;", "&mdash; only"),
  dd_sum$median_sim_dd_bb,
  ifelse(dd_sum$percentile > 0.3,
    "In other words: a downswing this size is <b>not statistically remarkable</b> for a player with your exact variance profile, even with zero behavioral change.",
    "That's a comparatively uncommon swing for your own return distribution &mdash; still explainable by variance, but on the unlucky side of it.")))
```

### 2. Posterior win rate by stake

```{r ds-post-table, eval=ds_ok}
pt <- wr_post %>% transmute(Stake = stake, Hands = n, `Raw bb/100` = sprintf("%+.1f", raw_bb100),
  `Posterior bb/100 (95% CI)` = sprintf("%+.1f  [%+.1f, %+.1f]", post_bb100, ci_lo, ci_hi),
  `P(true winner)` = percent(p_winner, 1))
knitr::kable(pt, align = "lrrrr",
  caption = "Bayesian posterior on true winrate, skeptical prior: normal, mean 0, SD 8 bb/100 (rake, no rakeback)")
```

```{r ds-post-table-rb, eval=ds_ok && has_rb_posterior}
pt_rb <- wr_post_rb %>% transmute(Stake = stake, Hands = n, `Raw bb/100` = sprintf("%+.1f", raw_bb100),
  `Posterior bb/100 (95% CI)` = sprintf("%+.1f  [%+.1f, %+.1f]", post_bb100, ci_lo, ci_hi),
  `P(true winner)` = percent(p_winner, 1))
knitr::kable(pt_rb, align = "lrrrr",
  caption = "Same posterior, WITH rakeback modeled in (see Rake & rakeback section for how)")
```

```{r ds-post-note, results='asis', eval=ds_ok}
ov <- wr_post[wr_post$stake == "overall", ]
verdict <- if (ov$p_winner < 0.2) {
  "probably not beating these games overall yet"
} else if (ov$p_winner < 0.5) {
  "unclear, more likely losing than winning"
} else if (ov$p_winner < 0.8) {
  "leaning toward a long-run winner, with a wide interval"
} else {
  "likely a long-run winner"
}
rb_line <- if (has_rb_posterior) {
  ov_rb <- wr_post_rb[wr_post_rb$stake == "overall", ]
  sprintf(' With rakeback folded in (below), P(winner) moves from %s to %s.',
          percent(ov$p_winner, 1), percent(ov_rb$p_winner, 1))
} else ""
cat(sprintf('<p class="meta"><b>Overall: %s</b> (P(true win rate &gt; 0) = %s, under a prior that assumes break-even until shown otherwise). The raw win rate and the posterior differ because the prior shrinks noisy estimates toward zero; per stake, the intervals show how far each estimate can move.%s</p>',
  verdict, percent(ov$p_winner, 1), rb_line))
```

### 3. Bankroll consequence: risk of ruin

```{r ds-ror-chart, eval=ds_ok, fig.height=3.8}
ror_cols <- c("pessimistic (CI low)" = red, "central (posterior mean)" = ink, "optimistic (CI high)" = green, "central + rakeback" = "#d9c48f")
plot_ly(ror, x = ~buyins, y = ~ror_pct, color = ~scenario, colors = ror_cols,
        type = "scatter", mode = "lines+markers", height = 340,
        hovertemplate = "%{y:.1f}% ruin at %{x} buy-ins<extra>%{fullData.name}</extra>") %>%
  layout(title = list(text = "Risk of ruin vs bankroll size, at three winrate scenarios", font = list(size = 13)),
         xaxis = list(title = "bankroll (100bb buy-ins)", gridcolor = grid),
         yaxis = list(title = "risk of ruin (%)", gridcolor = grid, range = c(0, 105)),
         legend = list(orientation = "h", y = -0.25), margin = list(t = 40)) %>%
  config(displaylogo = FALSE, modeBarButtonsToRemove = c("select2d", "lasso2d", "autoScale2d"))
```

```{r ds-ror-note, results='asis', eval=ds_ok}
under5 <- function(sc) {
  r <- ror[ror$scenario == sc & ror$ror_pct <= 5, ]
  if (nrow(r)) paste0("~", min(r$buyins), " buy-ins") else "none of the bankrolls shown"
}
cat(sprintf('<p class="meta">Bankroll needed for under 5%% risk of ruin: %s at the posterior mean, %s at the pessimistic end of the interval, %s at the optimistic end. At a win rate of zero or below, the ruin model says any finite bankroll eventually busts, which is its way of saying the edge isn&rsquo;t established.</p>',
  under5("central (posterior mean)"), under5("pessimistic (CI low)"), under5("optimistic (CI high)")))
```

```{r ds-missing, results='asis', eval=!ds_ok}
cat('<p class="meta">No downswing-simulator output found &mdash; run <code>Rscript downswing_sim.R</code> (render does this automatically).</p>')
```

## Recent form

Career averages move slowly, so a change in how you're playing *right now* hides in the pile.
This isolates your latest sessions so adjustments show up fast. (Sessions that run past midnight
land on the next calendar day.)

```{r recent-form}
recent <- cash %>% mutate(Day = as.Date(dt)) %>% group_by(Day) %>%
  summarise(Hands = n(), VPIP = percent(mean(vpip), 1), PFR = percent(mean(pfr), 1),
            `3-bet` = percent(sum(three_bet) / pmax(sum(vsopen_opp), 1), 1),
            `bb/100` = sprintf("%+.1f", sum(net_bb)/n()*100), Net = tt(sum(net)),
            Stakes = paste(sort(unique(paste0(sb, "/", bb))), collapse = ", "), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(Day)) %>% head(8)
knitr::kable(recent, align = "lrrrrrrl")
```

```{r rolling-style, fig.height=3.6}
co <- cash %>% arrange(dt); k <- 300
roll <- function(x) as.numeric(stats::filter(x, rep(1/k, k), sides = 1))
co$rv <- roll(co$vpip); co$rp <- roll(co$pfr); co$idx <- seq_len(nrow(co))
rr <- co %>% filter(!is.na(rv)) %>% transmute(idx, VPIP = rv, PFR = rp) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(VPIP, PFR))
ggplot(rr, aes(idx, value, color = name)) + geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(VPIP = "#9aa7b0", PFR = green)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent) +
  labs(title = sprintf("Rolling VPIP / PFR (%d-hand moving average)", k),
       x = "hand # (chronological)", y = NULL)
```

> The career line is the average of everything; the **right edge of this chart is who you are
> now**. A falling VPIP with a steady-or-rising PFR is a tightening, more-aggressive adjustment —
> the direction the scorecard wants. Watch that the change *sticks* over the next few sessions
> rather than snapping back.

## Positional analysis

The core of any hand review. Below: how often you enter (VPIP) and raise (PFR) by seat, and
your win rate there. Late positions should be looser and more profitable; the blinds lose
(they post dead money) — the question is *how much*.

```{r position-stats}
ps <- cash %>% group_by(Position = hero_pos) %>%
  summarise(Hands = n(), VPIP = percent(mean(vpip), 1), PFR = percent(mean(pfr), 1),
            `bb/100` = sprintf("%+.1f", sum(net_bb)/n()*100), Net = tt(sum(net)), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(ps, align = "lrrrrr")
```

```{r position-chart, fig.height=3.8}
pc <- cash %>% group_by(hero_pos) %>% summarise(bb100 = sum(net_bb)/n()*100, .groups = "drop")
ggplot(pc, aes(hero_pos, bb100, fill = bb100 >= 0)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) + geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = ink) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = green, `FALSE` = red), guide = "none") +
  labs(title = "Win rate by position (bb/100)", x = NULL, y = "bb/100")
```

```{r vpip-pfr-chart, fig.height=3.6}
vp <- cash %>% group_by(hero_pos) %>%
  summarise(VPIP = mean(vpip), PFR = mean(pfr), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_longer(c(VPIP, PFR))
ggplot(vp, aes(hero_pos, value, fill = name)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge", width = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(VPIP = "#9aa7b0", PFR = green)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent) +
  labs(title = "Preflop entry (VPIP) and raise (PFR) by position", x = NULL, y = NULL)
```

> A healthy 6-max preflop game tightens from the blinds/early seats to the button. Watch for
> a VPIP that's too flat across positions (playing too many hands up front) or blinds that
> bleed far more than the ~ −30 to −50 bb/100 that posting dead money costs.

### Preflop aggression by position

The decisions that drive most of your winrate: how often you **open** (raise first in), how
often you **3-bet** a raiser, and how often you **fold to a 3-bet** after opening.

```{r preflop-position}
pf <- cash %>% group_by(Position = hero_pos) %>%
  summarise(Hands = n(),
            `Open-raise %`   = percent(sum(open_raise)   / pmax(sum(rfi_opp), 1), 1),
            `3-bet %`        = percent(sum(three_bet)    / pmax(sum(vsopen_opp), 1), 1),
            `Fold to 3-bet %`= percent(sum(fold_to_3bet) / pmax(sum(ftb_opp), 1), 1),
            `(3-bet n)` = sum(vsopen_opp), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(pf, align = "lrrrrr")
```

```{r preflop-chart, fig.height=3.6}
pfl <- cash %>% group_by(hero_pos) %>%
  summarise(`Open-raise` = sum(open_raise) / pmax(sum(rfi_opp), 1),
            `3-bet`       = sum(three_bet) / pmax(sum(vsopen_opp), 1), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_longer(c(`Open-raise`, `3-bet`))
ggplot(pfl, aes(hero_pos, value, fill = name)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge", width = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`Open-raise` = green, `3-bet` = ink)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent) +
  labs(title = "Open-raise and 3-bet frequency by position", x = NULL, y = NULL)
```

> Benchmarks (reg, 6-max): open-raise rises from ~18% UTG to ~45%+ on the button; 3-bet ~7–9%
> overall, higher from the blinds and button; fold-to-3-bet ~40–55%. **Note the small 3-bet/
> fold-to-3-bet samples** — these stabilize as you add hands. Reading them now: directionally,
> are you opening too tight late or never 3-betting light?

## Out-of-range hands and their results

You can see *where* your stats sit and *how they move* - but not whether being off-range actually
costs you. We can't prove "high VPIP caused that loss" (variance is too loud for that). What we **can**
do is take the specific hands that pushed a stat out of range and show how they really turned out -
forked by stat. Anecdotal, but it puts dollars next to the numbers.

To do that, each voluntary hand is tagged against a **per-position opening range** (a standard 6-max
chart by hand strength - tight UTG, wide on the button, blinds defend loose):

- **Loose** - you voluntarily played a hand *outside* your seat's range (this is what inflates VPIP).
- **Passed** - it folded to you first-in and you folded a hand that *is* in your range (too tight - the steal you skipped).
- **In** - a standard, in-range voluntary hand.

<div class="warn"><div class="warn-title">How to read this (a v1 heuristic)</div>
The range is a positional baseline from a hand-strength formula (Chen, with a set-mining bump for
small pairs). It knows "should I generally play this hand from this seat" but <b>not</b> the full
facing-action picture yet (opening vs. flatting a raise vs. 3-betting vs. defending a blind are
different ranges). So treat the buckets as directional, not gospel - and the per-position widths are
yours to tune in <code>features_coinpoker.R</code> (<code>POS_OPEN</code>).</div>

### Results by entry type

```{r fork-summary}
bk <- function(d, label) data.frame(Bucket = label, Hands = nrow(d), Net = tt(sum(d$net)),
  `bb/100` = sprintf("%+.1f", bb100(d)), `Win %` = percent(mean(d$net > 0), 1), check.names = FALSE)
fork <- rbind(
  bk(filter(cash, range_dir == "in"),    "VPIP - in-range entries (baseline)"),
  bk(filter(cash, range_dir == "loose"), "VPIP - LOOSE entries (out of range)"),
  bk(filter(cash, open_raise == 1),      "PFR - opens (raise first in)"),
  bk(filter(cash, three_bet == 1),       "3-bet - your 3-bets"))
knitr::kable(fork, align = "lrrrr", row.names = FALSE)
```

> The fork that matters: your **loose entries** vs everything else. The two aggression buckets (opens,
> 3-bets) are where your edge should live - if those print and the loose entries bleed, the read is
> "keep the aggression, tighten the junk." A hand can sit in more than one row (you can open a loose
> hand), so this is three lenses, not a clean split.

### 3-bets: where the profit comes from

Where 3-bet profit comes from decides how far to trust it. A 3-bet earns two ways: villains **fold now** (clean, low-variance fold equity) or you **win
postflop** (real, but swingy). The split:

```{r tb-street}
tb <- filter(cash, three_bet == 1)
seg <- function(d, l) data.frame(Segment = l, Hands = nrow(d), Net = tt(sum(d$net)),
  `bb/100` = sprintf("%+.1f", bb100(d)), check.names = FALSE)
ts <- rbind(
  seg(filter(tb, !saw_flop & net > 0),  "Won preflop - villain folded (clean)"),
  seg(filter(tb, !saw_flop & net <= 0), "Folded to a 4-bet (cost)"),
  seg(filter(tb, saw_flop),             "Saw a flop - won/lost postflop (swingy)"))
knitr::kable(ts, align = "lrrr", row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r tb-foldout, include=FALSE}
tb_fold <- 100 * mean(!tb$saw_flop)
op_fold <- 100 * mean(!cash$saw_flop[cash$open_raise == 1])
```

<p class="meta">`r sprintf("3-bets take the pot preflop %.0f%% of the time; opens steal %.0f%%. %s of the %s total 3-bet result was earned postflop, across %d hands.", tb_fold, op_fold, tt(sum(tb$net[tb$saw_flop])), tt(sum(tb$net)), sum(tb$saw_flop))`</p>

> Fold-equity profit is reliable; postflop profit is high-variance and can regress. If most of the
> 3-bet profit is postflop, treat it as provisional. Against opponents who call 3-bets light, the
> standard adjustment is to value-3-bet bigger and bluff-3-bet less.

### 3-bets by opener position and size

Against a **tighter** opener you're 3-betting into a stronger range; sizing controls how much fold
equity you actually buy. Samples are ~50-75 per opener and thin once split by size - read as directional.

```{r tb-pos}
vp <- tb %>% filter(!is.na(vsopen_pos)) %>%
  group_by(`Opener` = factor(vsopen_pos, levels = pos_lv)) %>%
  summarise(`Your 3-bets` = n(), Net = tt(sum(net)), `bb/100` = sprintf("%+.1f", sum(net_bb) / n() * 100),
            `Won preflop` = percent(mean(!saw_flop & net > 0), 1), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(`Your 3-bets` >= 8)
knitr::kable(vp, align = "lrrrr", row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r tb-size}
tb$szb <- cut(tb$tb_ratio, c(0, 2.6, 3.4, Inf),
              labels = c("Small (under 2.6x open)", "Standard (2.6-3.4x)", "Big (over 3.4x)"))
sz <- tb %>% filter(!is.na(szb)) %>% group_by(`3-bet size` = szb) %>%
  summarise(`Your 3-bets` = n(), Net = tt(sum(net)), `bb/100` = sprintf("%+.1f", sum(net_bb) / n() * 100),
            `Villain folds` = percent(mean(!saw_flop), 1), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(sz, align = "lrrrr", row.names = FALSE)
```

<p class="meta">`r sprintf("Median 3-bet: %.1fx the open (~%.1f bb). A common size is 3x in position and 3.5-4x out of position; against callers, smaller 3-bets buy little fold equity and push the decision postflop.", median(tb$tb_ratio, na.rm = TRUE), median(tb$tb_to_bb, na.rm = TRUE))`</p>

### Loose entries, hand by hand

Your loose entries, by hand - what each one has cost (or made) and **how many VPIP points it adds**.
This is the literal price of the hands you probably know you shouldn't be opening.

```{r loose-cost}
loose <- filter(cash, range_dir == "loose"); n_cash <- nrow(cash)
lc <- loose %>% group_by(Hand = hand169) %>%
  summarise(`Times played` = n(), net = sum(net), bbv = sum(net_bb) / n() * 100, .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(net) %>% head(12) %>%
  transmute(Hand, `Times played`, Net = tt(net), `bb/100` = sprintf("%+.1f", bbv),
            `VPIP added` = sprintf("+%.1f pp", `Times played` / n_cash * 100))
knitr::kable(lc, align = "lrrrr", row.names = FALSE)
```

<p class="meta">`r sprintf("All loose entries together: %d hands, %s, %+.1f bb/100, and about +%.1f VPIP points (your VPIP would be ~%.1f%% without them).", nrow(loose), tt(sum(loose$net)), bb100(loose), nrow(loose)/n_cash*100, mean(cash$vpip)*100 - nrow(loose)/n_cash*100)`</p>

Your costliest loose entries up close (same card-review layout as your daily hands):

```{r loose-cards, results='asis'}
render_review_cards(loose %>% arrange(net) %>% head(4),
  flagger = function(r) sprintf("loose open: %s from %s is outside your range", r$hand169, as.character(r$hero_pos)))
```

#### Loose entries by line

Your VPIP example - "looser play means more spots I shouldn't be in, and I lose there" - made concrete.
Each loose hand is bucketed by the **deepest action it reached**, and split by **position**. The point
isn't that loose hands are bad on average; it's *where* they convert into losses.

```{r loose-line}
z <- function(x) coalesce(x, 0)
loose <- loose %>% mutate(
  line = case_when(
    !saw_flop ~ "Folded preflop (cheap)",
    z(river_call) > 0 ~ "Paid a river bet",
    z(turn_call)  > 0 ~ "Paid a turn bet",
    z(flop_call)  > 0 ~ "Paid a flop bet",
    z(hero_river_bet) > 0 | z(hero_turn_bet) > 0 | z(hero_flop_bet) > 0 ~ "Bet / raised (aggressed)",
    TRUE ~ "Checked down / gave up"),
  posc = case_when(is.na(hero_first_flop) ~ "no flop", hero_first_flop ~ "OOP", TRUE ~ "IP"))
ll <- loose %>% group_by(Line = line) %>%
  summarise(Hands = n(), Net = tt(sum(net)), `bb/100` = sprintf("%+.1f", sum(net_bb) / n() * 100),
            `Win %` = percent(mean(net > 0), 1), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(factor(Line, levels = c("Folded preflop (cheap)", "Paid a flop bet", "Paid a turn bet",
                                  "Paid a river bet", "Bet / raised (aggressed)", "Checked down / gave up")))
knitr::kable(ll, align = "lrrrr", row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r loose-pos}
lp <- loose %>% filter(posc != "no flop") %>% group_by(Position = posc) %>%
  summarise(Hands = n(), Net = tt(sum(net)), `bb/100` = sprintf("%+.1f", sum(net_bb) / n() * 100), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(lp, align = "lrrr", row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Loose hands that saw a flop, by position")
```

> Loose hands in position: `r sprintf("%+.0f bb/100", bb100(filter(loose, posc=='IP')))`; out of position: `r sprintf("%+.0f", bb100(filter(loose, posc=='OOP')))`. Folding a loose hand preflop costs nothing; playing it is what costs, and cold-calling in position followed by passive postflop play is a common way to lose.

#### Loose entries over time

A first cut at tracking a leak across sessions: bars = loose entries **per 100 hands** that day (a *rate*,
so a high-volume day isn't just a tall bar), line = the **cumulative** dollars they've cost. A flattening
line means you've stopped the bleed; a falling bar-rate means you're entering tighter.

```{r loose-time, eval=has_snaps}
day_tot <- cash %>% mutate(d = as.Date(dt)) %>% count(d, name = "hd")
lt <- loose %>% mutate(d = as.Date(dt)) %>% group_by(d) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), net = sum(net), .groups = "drop") %>% arrange(d) %>%
  left_join(day_tot, by = "d") %>% mutate(rate = n / hd * 100)
lt$cum <- cumsum(lt$net); lt$idx <- seq_len(nrow(lt)); lt$dlab <- format(lt$d, "%b %d")
plot_ly(lt, x = ~idx, height = 330) %>%
  add_bars(y = ~rate, name = "Loose / 100 hands", marker = list(color = "#cdd5da"),
           text = ~sprintf("%s<br>%d loose of %d hands", dlab, n, hd),
           hovertemplate = "%{text}<br>%{y:.1f} per 100<extra></extra>") %>%
  add_trace(y = ~cum, name = "Cumulative cost", yaxis = "y2", type = "scatter", mode = "lines+markers",
            line = list(color = red, width = 2.2), marker = list(color = red, size = 5),
            text = ~dlab, hovertemplate = "%{text}<br>cumulative %{y:.2f} T<extra></extra>") %>%
  layout(title = list(text = "Loose entries by session: rate per 100 hands (bars) and cumulative cost (line)",
                      font = list(size = 14, color = ink), x = 0.02),
         xaxis = list(title = "", tickmode = "array", tickvals = lt$idx, ticktext = lt$dlab,
                      tickangle = -40, tickfont = list(size = 10)),
         yaxis = list(title = "Loose entries / 100 hands"),
         yaxis2 = list(title = "Cumulative T", overlaying = "y", side = "right", showgrid = FALSE,
                       zeroline = TRUE, zerolinecolor = "#c9ced3"),
         legend = list(orientation = "h", x = 0, y = 1.12), hovermode = "x unified",
         margin = list(r = 62, t = 54))
```

### Button hands folded first in

Your button is a **net loser** despite being the seat that should print most - and the range model
says why: you're too tight first-in. When it folds to you on the BTN with a hand **inside** your
opening range, here's how often you fold it anyway, plus the hands you're passing up.

```{r btn-steal}
btn <- filter(cash, hero_pos == "BTN")
spots <- filter(btn, rfi_opp == 1, in_open_range)          # openable, in-range, folded to you
n_spots <- nrow(spots); n_passed <- sum(spots$range_dir == "passed", na.rm = TRUE)
btn_bb <- bb100(btn)
```

<p class="meta">`r sprintf("On the button, first-in with an in-range hand (%d spots), you folded %d of them - a %.0f%% pass rate on hands you're supposed to be opening. Button win rate overall: %+.1f bb/100.", n_spots, n_passed, 100*n_passed/max(n_spots,1), btn_bb)`</p>

```{r btn-passed}
bp <- btn %>% filter(range_dir == "passed") %>% count(Hand = hand169, name = "Times folded", sort = TRUE) %>% head(12)
knitr::kable(bp, align = "lr", row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Button hands you folded first-in that are inside your opening range")
```

> These are hands inside a standard button opening range that were folded first in. Folding them
> gives the blinds a walk; on the button the usual fix is to open them.

### Out-of-range days vs in-range days

The day-level version of "did it cost you": for each preflop stat, your bb/100 on days you were
**inside** the reg band vs **outside** it. Few days, high variance - read it as suggestive, not proof.

```{r day-band, eval=has_snaps}
band3 <- list(VPIP = bands$vpip, PFR = bands$pfr, `3-bet` = bands$threebet)
colmap <- c(VPIP = "vpip", PFR = "pfr", `3-bet` = "threebet")
db <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(band3), function(k) {
  b <- band3[[k]]; col <- colmap[[k]]; oob <- snaps[[col]] < b[1] | snaps[[col]] > b[2]
  mk <- function(sel, lab) { d <- snaps[sel, , drop = FALSE]; if (!nrow(d)) return(NULL)
    data.frame(Stat = k, Days = lab, `# days` = nrow(d), Hands = sum(d$n),
               `bb/100` = sprintf("%+.1f", sum(d$bb100 * d$n) / sum(d$n)), check.names = FALSE) }
  rbind(mk(!oob, "in band"), mk(oob, "out of band"))
}))
knitr::kable(db, align = "llrrr", row.names = FALSE)
```

## Postflop

What happens after the flop, where most of the money is actually won and lost. **C-bet** = how
often you continuation-bet the flop as the preflop aggressor; **fold-to-c-bet** = how often you
fold when *facing* one; **WWSF** (won-when-saw-flop) = how often you end the hand in profit once
you've seen a flop; **postflop AF** (aggression factor) = postflop bets+raises ÷ calls.

```{r postflop-kpis}
cb_pct  <- sum(cash$cbet_flop)    / pmax(sum(cash$cbet_opp), 1)
ftc_pct <- sum(cash$fold_to_cbet) / pmax(sum(cash$fcbet_opp), 1)
af      <- sum(cash$pf_aggr)      / pmax(sum(cash$pf_calls), 1)
wwsf    <- mean(cash$net[cash$saw_flop] > 0)
```

<div class="kpi-row">
<div class="kpi"><div class="kpi-label">C-bet flop</div><div class="kpi-value">`r percent(cb_pct, 0.1)`</div><div class="kpi-sub">as PF aggressor (n=`r sum(cash$cbet_opp)`)</div></div>
<div class="kpi"><div class="kpi-label">Fold to c-bet</div><div class="kpi-value">`r percent(ftc_pct, 0.1)`</div><div class="kpi-sub">facing a c-bet (n=`r sum(cash$fcbet_opp)`)</div></div>
<div class="kpi"><div class="kpi-label">Postflop AF</div><div class="kpi-value">`r sprintf("%.2f", af)`</div><div class="kpi-sub">bets+raises / calls</div></div>
<div class="kpi"><div class="kpi-label">WWSF</div><div class="kpi-value">`r percent(wwsf, 0.1)`</div><div class="kpi-sub">won when saw flop</div></div>
</div>

> Benchmarks (reg, 6-max): c-bet flop ~50–65%; fold-to-c-bet ~45–55% (folding much more is
> exploitable: opponents can bet any two cards); postflop AF ~2–3; WWSF ~45–50%. Here: c-bet
> `r percent(cb_pct, 0.1)`, fold-to-c-bet `r percent(ftc_pct, 0.1)` (n=`r sum(cash$fcbet_opp)`), AF `r sprintf("%.2f", af)`.

### The street funnel

How a hand narrows from dealt cards to showdown. Each bar is the share of **all** hands that
reach that street — the drop-offs show how often you fold vs. carry on.

```{r street-funnel, fig.height=3.4}
fn <- tibble::tibble(
  stage = factor(c("Entered pot (VPIP)", "Saw flop", "Saw turn", "Saw river", "Showdown"),
                 levels = rev(c("Entered pot (VPIP)", "Saw flop", "Saw turn", "Saw river", "Showdown"))),
  pct = c(mean(cash$vpip), mean(cash$saw_flop), mean(cash$saw_turn),
          mean(cash$saw_river), mean(cash$showdown)))
ggplot(fn, aes(stage, pct)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.65, fill = green) + coord_flip() +
  geom_text(aes(label = percent(pct, 0.1)), hjust = -0.15, size = 3.6, color = ink) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent, limits = c(0, max(fn$pct) * 1.15), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(title = "Street funnel: share of all hands reaching each street", x = NULL, y = NULL)
```

> The funnel shows how hands narrow street by street. One that stays wide to the river can mean too many
> loose calls; one that collapses fast can mean over-folding.

### Postflop by position

C-bet, fold-to-c-bet and WWSF by seat. Postflop samples are **much** smaller than preflop ones
(you have to reach the flop first), so read these as directional until they fill in.

```{r postflop-position}
pp <- cash %>% group_by(Position = hero_pos) %>%
  summarise(`Saw flop` = sum(saw_flop),
            `C-bet %`        = percent(sum(cbet_flop)    / pmax(sum(cbet_opp), 1), 1),
            `(C-bet n)`      = sum(cbet_opp),
            `Fold to c-bet %`= percent(sum(fold_to_cbet) / pmax(sum(fcbet_opp), 1), 1),
            `(n)`            = sum(fcbet_opp),
            `WWSF %`         = percent(mean(net[saw_flop] > 0), 1), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(pp, align = "lrrrrrr")
```

```{r postflop-position-chart, fig.height=3.6}
ppl <- cash %>% group_by(hero_pos) %>%
  summarise(`C-bet` = sum(cbet_flop) / pmax(sum(cbet_opp), 1),
            `Fold to c-bet` = sum(fold_to_cbet) / pmax(sum(fcbet_opp), 1), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_longer(c(`C-bet`, `Fold to c-bet`))
ggplot(ppl, aes(hero_pos, value, fill = name)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge", width = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`C-bet` = green, `Fold to c-bet` = "#9aa7b0")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent) +
  labs(title = "C-bet and fold-to-c-bet frequency by position", x = NULL, y = NULL)
```

## Starting hands

How your results break down by what you were dealt. Note: bb/100 here means **bb won per
100 hands *of that type*** — a selection/value metric, not a sustained win rate (e.g. pocket
pairs print because of set-mining, but you're only dealt one ~6% of the time).

```{r hand-groups}
# expected dealt frequency per group, from combinatorics over all 1326 two-card combos
ref <- expand.grid(hi = 2:14, lo = 2:14); ref <- ref[ref$hi >= ref$lo, ]
ref <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(ref)), function(i) {
  a <- ref$hi[i]; b <- ref$lo[i]
  if (a == b) data.frame(hi = a, lo = b, pair = TRUE,  suited = FALSE, combos = 6)
  else  rbind(data.frame(hi = a, lo = b, pair = FALSE, suited = TRUE,  combos = 4),
              data.frame(hi = a, lo = b, pair = FALSE, suited = FALSE, combos = 12)) }))
.prem <- (ref$pair & ref$hi >= 10) | (ref$hi == 14 & ref$lo == 13)
.brd  <- !ref$pair & ref$hi >= 10 & ref$lo >= 10
ref$grp <- ifelse(.prem, "Premium (TT+, AK)", ifelse(ref$pair, "Other pair", ifelse(.brd, "Broadway",
  ifelse(ref$suited & (ref$hi - ref$lo) <= 3 & ref$lo >= 5, "Suited connector",
  ifelse(ref$suited, "Other suited", "Other offsuit")))))
expg <- ref %>% group_by(grp) %>% summarise(exp_pct = sum(combos) / 1326, .groups = "drop")

nd <- nrow(cash)
hg <- cash %>% group_by(grp) %>%
  summarise(Dealt = n(), played = mean(vpip), net = sum(net), bb100 = sum(net_bb)/n()*100, .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(expg, by = "grp") %>% arrange(desc(bb100)) %>%
  transmute(`Hand group` = grp, Dealt,
            `Dealt %` = percent(Dealt/nd, 0.1), `Expected %` = percent(exp_pct, 0.1),
            `Played %` = percent(played, 1), `bb/100` = sprintf("%+.1f", bb100), Net = tt(net))
knitr::kable(hg, align = "lrrrrrr")
```

```{r hand-cat-chart, fig.height=3.4}
hc <- cash %>% group_by(cat) %>% summarise(bb100 = sum(net_bb)/n()*100, hands = n(), .groups = "drop")
ggplot(hc, aes(reorder(cat, bb100), bb100, fill = bb100 >= 0)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6) + geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = ink) + coord_flip() +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%+.1f", bb100)), hjust = ifelse(hc$bb100 >= 0, -0.1, 1.1), size = 3.4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = green, `FALSE` = red), guide = "none") +
  labs(title = "Win rate by hand type (bb/100)", x = NULL, y = "bb/100")
```

### Card luck: dealt vs expected

Which cards you're dealt is pure chance: over a big sample you should see each hand type at a
fixed rate the math fixes in advance. Comparing what you were **dealt** to what's **expected**
separates *running bad* from *playing bad* — if you're under-dealt premiums, a soft stretch isn't
your fault. (Frequencies are over non-bomb hands; the deck doesn't care, so expectations still hold.)

```{r card-luck-cat}
exp_cat <- c(`Pocket pair` = 78/1326, Suited = 312/1326, Offsuit = 936/1326)
obs <- table(factor(cash$cat, levels = names(exp_cat)))
clk <- data.frame(Type = names(exp_cat), Dealt = as.integer(obs),
  `Dealt %` = percent(as.numeric(obs)/sum(obs), 0.1), `Expected %` = percent(exp_cat, 0.1),
  check.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(clk, align = "lrrr")
pval <- suppressWarnings(chisq.test(as.integer(obs), p = exp_cat)$p.value)
```

Overall your dealt distribution is **`r if (pval < 0.05) "skewed vs expected" else "statistically normal"`**
(chi-square p = `r sprintf("%.2f", pval)`) — `r if (pval < 0.05) "an unusual run." else "no meaningful card bias; deviations are ordinary noise."`
The interesting part is the **premium hands**, where small counts swing your results most:

```{r card-luck-premium, fig.height=3.4}
rch2 <- setNames(c(as.character(2:9), "T", "J", "Q", "K", "A"), 2:14)
cash$hand <- ifelse(cash$pair, paste0(rch2[as.character(cash$hi)], rch2[as.character(cash$hi)]),
  paste0(rch2[as.character(cash$hi)], rch2[as.character(cash$lo)], ifelse(cash$suited, "s", "o")))
keys <- c("AA","KK","QQ","JJ","TT","AKs","AKo","AQs")
combos <- function(hd) if (substr(hd,1,1)==substr(hd,2,2) & nchar(hd)==2) 6 else if (endsWith(hd,"s")) 4 else 12
kl <- lapply(keys, function(hd){
  d <- cash[cash$hand==hd, ]; e <- nd*combos(hd)/1326
  data.frame(Hand=hd, Dealt=nrow(d), Expected=round(e,1),
             Luck=sprintf("%+.0f%%", (nrow(d)/e-1)*100), Net=tt(sum(d$net)),
             `bb/100`=sprintf("%+.1f", ifelse(nrow(d)>0, sum(d$net_bb)/nrow(d)*100, 0)), check.names=FALSE) })
kl <- do.call(rbind, kl)
knitr::kable(kl, align="lrrrrr", caption="Premium hands: dealt vs expected, and how they've paid (small samples , directional)")

klp <- kl %>% transmute(Hand=factor(Hand, levels=keys), Dealt=as.numeric(Dealt), Expected=as.numeric(Expected)) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(Dealt, Expected))
ggplot(klp, aes(Hand, value, fill=name)) +
  geom_col(position="dodge", width=0.7) +
  scale_fill_manual(values=c(Dealt=green, Expected="#9aa7b0")) +
  labs(title="Premium hands dealt vs expected", x=NULL, y="count")
```

> Card luck explains *swings*, not your *win rate* — over a full sample it washes out to zero.
> Use it to stay sane during downswings ("am I actually getting hands?"), not to excuse leaks.
> The money you make *with* the premiums you're dealt (the Net column) is the part skill controls.

### RNG audit

Different question from the section above: not "did I run good," but "does CoinPoker's shuffle
itself look like a fair 52-card deck?" Chi-square goodness-of-fit on rank, suit, and specific-card
frequency, for both hole cards and (single-board) community cards, plus binomial checks on the
pocket-pair and suited rates against their fixed combinatorial odds. Standalone + wired into every
render (`rng_audit.R`).

```{r rng-load}
rng <- tryCatch(read.csv("coinpoker_rng_audit.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE), error = function(e) NULL)
```

```{r rng-table, eval=!is.null(rng)}
rt <- rng %>% transmute(Test = test, `chi-sq` = ifelse(is.na(statistic), "-", sprintf("%.2f", statistic)),
                         df = ifelse(is.na(df), "-", as.character(df)), `p-value` = sprintf("%.3f", p_value), n)
knitr::kable(rt, align = "lrrrr", caption = "RNG audit: dealt frequencies vs a uniform, fair deck")
```

```{r rng-note, results='asis', eval=!is.null(rng)}
n_sig <- sum(rng$p_value < 0.05)
cat(sprintf('<p class="meta">%d of %d tests fall below p=0.05 &mdash; with this many tests, about %.1f "significant" hits are expected from a perfectly fair deck by chance alone, so %s. %s</p>',
  n_sig, nrow(rng), 0.05 * nrow(rng),
  ifelse(n_sig <= 1, "this is exactly what a fair shuffle looks like", "there are more hits than chance alone predicts, worth revisiting with more hands"),
  ifelse(n_sig <= 1, "No evidence of a biased deck.", "Not proof of unfairness either &mdash; just a flag to keep watching.")))
```

```{r rng-missing, results='asis', eval=is.null(rng)}
cat('<p class="meta">No <code>coinpoker_rng_audit.csv</code> found &mdash; run <code>Rscript rng_audit.R</code> (render does this automatically).</p>')
```

### The hand grid

Every one of the 169 starting hands, laid out like a range chart — **pairs on the diagonal,
suited upper-right, offsuit lower-left**. Shading = how often you **played** that holding
(VPIP). This is your actual playing range; gaps and over-plays jump out immediately. Add more
hands and it fills in and stabilizes.

```{r hand-grid, fig.height=5.6}
rch <- setNames(c(as.character(2:9), "T", "J", "Q", "K", "A"), 2:14)   # 14->A
lab <- function(rI, cI) {                                              # cell (row,col) -> "AKs"
  rhi <- 15 - pmin(rI, cI); rlo <- 15 - pmax(rI, cI)                   # rank values
  ifelse(rI == cI, paste0(rch[as.character(15 - rI)], rch[as.character(15 - rI)]),
         paste0(rch[as.character(rhi)], rch[as.character(rlo)], ifelse(cI > rI, "s", "o")))
}
full <- expand.grid(row = 1:13, col = 1:13)
full$hand <- mapply(lab, full$row, full$col)

agg <- cash %>%
  mutate(row = ifelse(pair, 15 - hi, ifelse(suited, 15 - hi, 15 - lo)),
         col = ifelse(pair, 15 - hi, ifelse(suited, 15 - lo, 15 - hi))) %>%
  group_by(row, col) %>% summarise(dealt = n(), played = mean(vpip), net = sum(net), .groups = "drop")
g <- left_join(full, agg, by = c("row", "col"))
ranks <- c("A","K","Q","J","T","9","8","7","6","5","4","3","2")

ggplot(g, aes(col, row, fill = played)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_text(aes(label = hand), size = 2.3, color = "#33414a") +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#f4f7fa", high = green, na.value = "#fafbfb",
                      labels = percent, name = "played %") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:13, labels = ranks, position = "top", expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_reverse(breaks = 1:13, labels = ranks, expand = c(0, 0)) +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(title = "Starting-hand grid: shaded by how often you played it", x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank())
```

```{r hand-extremes}
he <- cash %>% group_by(hand = ifelse(pair, paste0(rch[as.character(hi)], rch[as.character(hi)]),
                  paste0(rch[as.character(hi)], rch[as.character(lo)], ifelse(suited, "s", "o")))) %>%
  summarise(dealt = n(), played = percent(mean(vpip), 1), net = sum(net), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(dealt >= 8)
knitr::kable(bind_rows(
  he %>% slice_max(net, n = 5) %>% mutate(group = "Most profitable"),
  he %>% slice_min(net, n = 5) %>% mutate(group = "Most costly")) %>%
  transmute(Group = group, Hand = hand, Dealt = dealt, `Played` = played, Net = tt(net)),
  align = "llrrr", caption = "Best/worst specific hands (>=8 times dealt; noisy, directional only)")
```

## Showdown

```{r showdown}
saw <- filter(cash, saw_flop)
wtsd <- mean(saw$showdown)
wsd  <- mean(cash$net[cash$showdown] > 0)
```

<div class="kpi-row">
<div class="kpi"><div class="kpi-label">WTSD</div><div class="kpi-value">`r percent(wtsd, 0.1)`</div><div class="kpi-sub">saw flop → showdown</div></div>
<div class="kpi"><div class="kpi-label">W$SD</div><div class="kpi-value">`r percent(wsd, 0.1)`</div><div class="kpi-sub">showdowns won</div></div>
<div class="kpi"><div class="kpi-label">Saw flop</div><div class="kpi-value">`r percent(mean(cash$saw_flop), 0.1)`</div><div class="kpi-sub">of all hands</div></div>
</div>

### Made hands at showdown

The hand you actually made at showdown, how often you make each, and the money it wins or loses.
This is where loose-passive play shows its bill: strong hands print, but showing down weak ones
(one pair, ace-high) bleeds it back.

```{r made-hands}
ord <- c("High Card","One Pair","Two Pair","Three Of A Kind","Straight","Flush","Full House","Four Of A Kind","Straight Flush")
sd <- cash %>% filter(showdown, !is.na(sd_cat))
mh <- sd %>% group_by(sd_cat) %>%
  summarise(`Showdowns` = n(), `Won %` = percent(mean(net > 0), 1),
            `Net` = tt(sum(net)), `Avg/hand` = tt(mean(net)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(sd_cat = factor(sd_cat, levels = ord)) %>% arrange(sd_cat) %>%
  rename(`Made hand` = sd_cat)
knitr::kable(mh, align = "lrrrr")
```

```{r made-hands-chart, fig.height=3.4}
mc <- sd %>% group_by(sd_cat) %>% summarise(net = sum(net), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(sd_cat = factor(sd_cat, levels = ord))
ggplot(mc, aes(sd_cat, net, fill = net >= 0)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) + geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = ink) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = green, `FALSE` = red), guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0("$", x)) +
  labs(title = "Net by made hand at showdown", x = NULL, y = "net ($)") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 20, hjust = 1))
```

### Hands that beat Hero at showdown

The flip side: when you lose a showdown the winner has to table their hand, so we know exactly
what you're paying off. The split tells you *which* leak — losing to **better one pair** means
kicker/second-pair calldowns (outkicked); losing to **two pair+** means refusing to fold a strong-
but-beaten hand to obvious aggression.

```{r what-beats-you}
ordv <- c("High Card","One Pair","Two Pair","Three Of A Kind","Straight","Flush","Full House","Four Of A Kind","Straight Flush")
loss <- cash %>% filter(showdown, net < 0, !is.na(villain_cat))
wb <- loss %>% group_by(villain_cat) %>%
  summarise(`Times` = n(), `$ lost` = tt(sum(net)), `Avg` = tt(mean(net)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(villain_cat = factor(villain_cat, levels = ordv)) %>% arrange(villain_cat) %>%
  rename(`Beaten by` = villain_cat)
knitr::kable(wb, align = "lrrr")
```

When you specifically held **one pair** and lost — your most common and most expensive showdown —
here's what beat you:

```{r one-pair-matchup}
op <- cash %>% filter(showdown, net < 0, sd_cat == "One Pair", !is.na(villain_cat))
opm <- op %>% mutate(villain_cat = factor(villain_cat, levels = ordv)) %>%
  group_by(`Beaten by` = villain_cat) %>%
  summarise(Times = n(), `$ lost` = tt(sum(net)), .groups = "drop") %>% arrange(`Beaten by`)
knitr::kable(opm, align = "lrr")
op_kick <- op %>% filter(villain_cat == "One Pair"); op_2p <- op %>% filter(villain_cat == "Two Pair")
```

> Two readings, both foldable: **`r nrow(op_kick)` of your one-pair losses (`r tt(sum(op_kick$net))`)
> were to a *better one pair*** — outkicked, i.e. calling with a dominated pair/kicker — and
> **`r nrow(op_2p)` (`r tt(sum(op_2p$net))`) were to two pair**, i.e. paying off made strength.
> The first is a preflop/flop hand-selection fix; the second is a turn/river discipline fix.

### Calls made when likely behind

A proxy for the "I knew I was beat but called anyway" leak: chips you **called on the turn and
river in hands you lost**. It isn't pure (some were correct calls that lost, some turn calls were
draws) — but at volume it's a strong signal for over-calling. River calls that lost are the
cleanest read: the river is a pure bluff-catch, so paying it off and losing means you were behind.

```{r paying-off}
lost <- filter(cash, net < 0)
river_paid <- sum(lost$river_call); turn_paid <- sum(lost$turn_call)
n_river <- sum(lost$river_call > 0); n_turn <- sum(lost$turn_call > 0)
```

<div class="kpi-row">
<div class="kpi"><div class="kpi-label">River calls that lost</div><div class="kpi-value neg">`r tt(river_paid)`</div><div class="kpi-sub">`r n_river` hands paid off on the river</div></div>
<div class="kpi"><div class="kpi-label">Turn calls that lost</div><div class="kpi-value neg">`r tt(turn_paid)`</div><div class="kpi-sub">`r n_turn` hands, includes missed draws</div></div>
<div class="kpi"><div class="kpi-label">Combined</div><div class="kpi-value neg">`r tt(river_paid + turn_paid)`</div><div class="kpi-sub">vs total net `r tt(sum(cash$net))`</div></div>
</div>

<p class="meta">Folding even a fraction of these spots swings more than your whole net result. Not every
call here was a mistake — but the size of the number relative to your bottom line is the point:
big turn/river bluff-catches are the cheapest leak to plug.</p>

#### River calls by bet size (share of the pot)

This is the poker-accurate cut: the villain's river bet as a fraction of the pot it was bet into
(reconstructed action by action and checked against the hand-history totals). Bet sizing signals
*how polarized* a betting range is — and which sizes you're profitably bluff-catching vs. paying off.

```{r call-size}
rc <- cash %>% filter(river_call > 0, !is.na(river_pot), river_pot > river_call) %>%
  mutate(betpot = river_call / (river_pot - river_call),
         bucket = cut(betpot, c(0, 0.4, 0.7, 1.1, Inf),
                      labels = c("<= 1/3 pot", "~1/2 pot", "~full pot", "overbet")))
cs <- rc %>% group_by(`Villain river bet` = bucket) %>%
  summarise(Calls = n(), `Won %` = percent(mean(net > 0), 1), Net = tt(sum(net)),
            `Avg/call` = tt(mean(net)), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(cs, align = "lrrrr")
```

```{r call-size-chart, fig.height=3.2}
# NOTE order matters: compute `won` from the row-level net BEFORE the `net = sum(net)`
# summary shadows the column (else mean(net>0) reads the scalar sum -> bogus 0%/100%).
csc <- rc %>% group_by(bucket) %>% summarise(won = mean(net > 0), n = n(), net = sum(net), .groups = "drop")
ggplot(csc, aes(bucket, net, fill = net >= 0)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.65) + geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = ink) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.0f%% won (n=%d)", won * 100, n)),
            vjust = ifelse(csc$net >= 0, -0.4, 1.2), size = 3.3, color = ink) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = green, `FALSE` = red), guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0("$", x)) +
  labs(title = "River calls: net by villain bet size (% of pot)", x = NULL, y = "net ($)")
```

> Overbets (`r csc$n[csc$bucket=="overbet"]` calls, `r percent(csc$won[csc$bucket=="overbet"],1)` won) come from a polarized range, nearly
> all strong hands or air, and at low stakes they skew strong. Tiny bets (a third of the pot or less) are
> often thin value. Compare the won share at each size to the price: a size that loses at its price is
> one to call less often against.

### Biggest losses

Your costliest single hands, with the turn/river you called and what you ended up holding. Sort
your memory against these: the ones with a big river call and a weak made hand are the reviewable
ones.

```{r biggest-losses}
bl <- cash %>% arrange(net) %>% head(10) %>%
  transmute(Net = tt(net), Hand = hero_cards, Pos = as.character(hero_pos),
            `Turn call` = tt(turn_call), `River call` = tt(river_call),
            `You made` = ifelse(is.na(sd_cat), "no showdown", sd_cat),
            `Lost to` = ifelse(is.na(villain_cards), "-",
                               paste0(villain_cards, " (", villain_cat, ")")))
knitr::kable(bl, align = "rllrrll")
```

## Draws and set-mining

The question behind your one-pair/ace-high losses: how much were busted draws, are you paying too
much to chase, and how much of your win comes from *getting there* (hitting draws, flopping sets)
rather than from value? This reconstructs the board on every hand to flag flush/straight draws and
whether they completed. (Single-board hands only; a "draw" = flush or open/gutshot straight draw
on the flop or turn that wasn't already a made straight/flush.)

```{r draws-calc}
rkv <- setNames(2:14, c(as.character(2:9), "T", "J", "Q", "K", "A"))
cardsplit <- function(s) if (is.na(s) || s == "") character(0) else str_extract_all(s, "[2-9TJQKA][cdhs]")[[1]]
csuit <- function(c) substr(c, 2, 2); crank <- function(c) rkv[substr(c, 1, 1)]
has_flush <- function(allc, hero) any(vapply(c("c","d","h","s"), function(s) sum(csuit(allc)==s) >= 5 && any(csuit(hero)==s), logical(1)))
has_straight <- function(allc, hero) {
  r <- unique(crank(allc)); if (14 %in% r) r <- c(r, 1); hr <- unique(crank(hero)); if (14 %in% hr) hr <- c(hr, 1)
  any(vapply(1:10, function(lo) { w <- lo:(lo+4); all(w %in% r) && any(w %in% hr) }, logical(1)))
}
draw_here <- function(allc, hero) {
  fd <- any(vapply(c("c","d","h","s"), function(s) sum(csuit(allc)==s)==4 && any(csuit(hero)==s), logical(1)))
  r <- unique(crank(allc)); if (14 %in% r) r <- c(r, 1); hr <- unique(crank(hero)); if (14 %in% hr) hr <- c(hr, 1)
  sd <- any(vapply(1:10, function(lo) { w <- lo:(lo+4); sum(w %in% r)==4 && any(w %in% hr) }, logical(1)))
  fd || sd
}
sb <- cash %>% filter(saw_flop, !is.na(flop), nchar(hero_cards) >= 4)
od <- hit <- logical(nrow(sb))
for (i in seq_len(nrow(sb))) {
  hero <- cardsplit(sb$hero_cards[i]); fl <- cardsplit(sb$flop[i])
  tn <- cardsplit(sb$turn_card[i]); rv <- cardsplit(sb$river_card[i])
  if (length(hero) < 2 || length(fl) < 3) next
  fb <- c(hero, fl); tb <- c(fb, tn); full <- c(tb, rv)
  made_flop <- has_flush(fb, hero) || has_straight(fb, hero)
  od[i]  <- (draw_here(fb, hero) || (length(tn) > 0 && draw_here(tb, hero))) && !made_flop
  hit[i] <- has_flush(full, hero) || has_straight(full, hero)
}
sb$on_draw <- od; sb$hit <- hit
dr <- filter(sb, on_draw)
d_hit <- sum(dr$net[dr$hit]); d_miss <- sum(dr$net[!dr$hit])
chased <- sum(dr$turn_call + dr$river_call)
busted_sd <- sb %>% filter(showdown, sd_cat %in% c("One Pair","High Card"), on_draw, !hit)

# set-mining
hc <- lapply(cash$hero_cards, cardsplit)
cash$pp  <- vapply(hc, function(x) length(x)==2 && substr(x[1],1,1)==substr(x[2],1,1), logical(1))
cash$ppr <- vapply(hc, function(x) if (length(x)==2 && substr(x[1],1,1)==substr(x[2],1,1)) substr(x[1],1,1) else NA_character_, character(1))
ppf <- cash %>% filter(pp, saw_flop, !is.na(flop))
ppf$set <- mapply(function(r, f) sum(substr(cardsplit(f), 1, 1) == r) >= 1, ppf$ppr, ppf$flop)
pp_net <- sum(cash$net[cash$pp]); set_net <- sum(ppf$net[ppf$set])
```

### Set-mining

<div class="kpi-row">
<div class="kpi"><div class="kpi-label">Flopped a set</div><div class="kpi-value">`r percent(mean(ppf$set), 1)`</div><div class="kpi-sub">`r sum(ppf$set)` of `r nrow(ppf)` pairs that saw a flop (~12% is normal)</div></div>
<div class="kpi"><div class="kpi-label">Net from sets</div><div class="kpi-value pos">`r tt(set_net)`</div><div class="kpi-sub">just `r sum(ppf$set)` hands</div></div>
<div class="kpi"><div class="kpi-label">Pocket-pair net</div><div class="kpi-value `r if(pp_net>=0) "pos" else "neg"`">`r tt(pp_net)`</div><div class="kpi-sub">`r tt(pp_net - set_net)` without the sets</div></div>
</div>

> Sets are **`r percent(set_net/pp_net, 1)` of pocket-pair profit**. Set-mining is a repeatable edge,
> but it depends on the preflop call being small relative to stacks (implied odds); small pairs facing big
> raises without deep stacks are folds.

### Draws: hit, missed, and taken to showdown

<div class="kpi-row">
<div class="kpi"><div class="kpi-label">On a draw</div><div class="kpi-value">`r percent(mean(sb$on_draw), 1)`</div><div class="kpi-sub">of flops seen (flush/straight draw)</div></div>
<div class="kpi"><div class="kpi-label">Hit by river</div><div class="kpi-value">`r percent(mean(dr$hit), 1)`</div><div class="kpi-sub">`r sum(dr$hit)` of `r nrow(dr)` draws got there</div></div>
<div class="kpi"><div class="kpi-label">Draw net (hit − miss)</div><div class="kpi-value `r if(sum(dr$net)>=0) "pos" else "neg"`">`r tt(sum(dr$net))`</div><div class="kpi-sub">`r tt(d_hit)` hit, `r tt(d_miss)` missed</div></div>
</div>

> Drawing hands win **`r tt(d_hit)`** when they get there and lose **`r tt(d_miss)`** when they don't, **`r tt(sum(dr$net))`**
> in all; near break-even is how draws are supposed to net out. The leak to check is the back end:
> **`r nrow(busted_sd)`** One-Pair or High-Card showdowns were busted draws taken to showdown, for
> **`r tt(sum(busted_sd$net))`**. A missed draw with ace-high or bottom pair is usually a give-up or a bluff, not a call.

## Bet sizing

Sizing carries information. *Playing hands backwards* from showdowns, we can read what villains'
river sizes mean — and check whether your own sizing leaks your hand strength. (River only; samples
are small, so read these as signals to test at the table, not settled facts.)

```{r betsize-calc}
made_str <- function(hole, board) {
  if (length(hole) < 2 || length(board) < 5) return(NA_character_)
  allc <- c(hole, board)
  if (has_flush(allc, hole) || has_straight(allc, hole)) return("value")
  rk <- table(crank(allc))
  if (max(rk) >= 3 || sum(rk >= 2) >= 2) return("value")
  if (sum(rk >= 2) == 1) return("one pair")
  "bluff"
}
hb <- cash %>% filter(hero_river_bet > 0, !is.na(hero_river_pot), hero_river_pot > 0,
                      !is.na(flop), !is.na(river_card), nchar(hero_cards) >= 4) %>%
  mutate(betpot = hero_river_bet / hero_river_pot, called = showdown,
         size = cut(betpot, c(0, 0.4, 0.7, Inf),
                    labels = c("small (<= 1/3 pot)", "medium (~1/2 pot)", "big (>= 2/3 pot)")))
hb$strength <- mapply(function(hc, fl, tc, rc) made_str(cardsplit(hc),
                      c(cardsplit(fl), cardsplit(tc), cardsplit(rc))),
                      hb$hero_cards, hb$flop, hb$turn_card, hb$river_card)
vs <- cash %>% filter(river_call > 0, !is.na(river_pot), river_pot > river_call, !is.na(villain_cat)) %>%
  mutate(vbetpot = river_call / (river_pot - river_call),
         vstrength = factor(ifelse(villain_cat %in% c("Two Pair","Three Of A Kind","Straight","Flush","Full House"),
                            "value (2pair+)", ifelse(villain_cat == "One Pair", "one pair", "bluff (high card)")),
                            levels = c("bluff (high card)", "one pair", "value (2pair+)")))
mm <- str_match(cash$hero_cards, "([2-9TJQKA]).\\s?([2-9TJQKA]).")
cash$akq <- (mm[,2] == "A" & mm[,3] %in% c("K","Q")) | (mm[,3] == "A" & mm[,2] %in% c("K","Q"))
akq <- filter(cash, akq)
```

### Opponents' river sizing by hand shown

For every river you called and they tabled a hand, their bet size vs. what they actually had:

```{r villain-size}
vt <- vs %>% group_by(`Villain showed` = vstrength) %>%
  summarise(Hands = n(), `Median bet (x pot)` = sprintf("%.2f", median(vbetpot)),
            `Your net` = tt(sum(net)), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(vt, align = "lrrr")
```

> Read villain river sizes by what they showed: if bluffs cluster at certain sizes and value at others,
> that size is a tell for calling or folding. Samples here are small, so treat any pattern as a working
> read. **AK/AQ:** `r tt(sum(akq$net))`, `r sprintf("%+.1f", sum(akq$net_bb)/nrow(akq)*100)` bb/100 over `r nrow(akq)` hands; top pair with a top
> kicker is still one pair, and the losses usually come from paying off two pair.

### Hero's river sizing and results

```{r my-river-size}
mr <- hb %>% group_by(`Your bet size` = size) %>%
  summarise(Bets = n(), `Folded them out %` = percent(mean(!called), 1),
            Net = tt(sum(net)), `Avg/bet` = tt(mean(net)), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(mr, align = "lrrrr")
```

Your river betting is a **strength** overall (`r tt(sum(hb$net))` across `r nrow(hb)` bets) — bigger
bets fold villains out more often, and every size is in the black. The question is whether it's
*balanced*, which is the next table.

### River bet size vs hand strength

```{r my-river-tell}
st <- hb %>% filter(!is.na(strength)) %>% group_by(`Your bet size` = size) %>%
  summarise(Bets = n(), `Bluff %` = percent(mean(strength == "bluff"), 1),
            `One pair %` = percent(mean(strength == "one pair"), 1),
            `Value (2pair+) %` = percent(mean(strength == "value"), 1), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(st, align = "lrrrr")
```

> If big river bets are almost always value, the betting range is face-up: a thinking opponent folds to
> them for free. Missed draws are the natural hands to balance them with, as bluffs instead of calls.

### Busted draws on the river

You've been trying to turn missed draws into river bluffs. The trap: a bluff that **works** shows up
as "won, no showdown" - you never reveal the busted hand - so counting *shown* bluffs undercounts
badly. Board reconstruction fixes that: of the hands where you **reached the river with a busted draw**,
how often did you **bet it** (the adjustment) vs **call** (the old leak) vs check/give up - counted
whether or not it got called. Earlier vs recent (median-date split).

```{r busted-river}
br <- sb %>% filter(on_draw, !hit, saw_river)
br$act <- ifelse(coalesce(br$hero_river_bet, 0) > 0, "Bet it (bluff)",
          ifelse(coalesce(br$river_call, 0) > 0, "Called (paid off)", "Checked / gave up"))
br$era <- ifelse(as.Date(br$dt) >= median(as.Date(br$dt)), "recent", "earlier")
bet_share <- function(e) mean(br$act[br$era == e] == "Bet it (bluff)")
brt <- br %>% group_by(Era = factor(era, c("earlier", "recent"))) %>%
  summarise(`Busted-draw rivers` = n(),
            `Bet (bluff) %` = percent(mean(act == "Bet it (bluff)"), 1),
            `Called %` = percent(mean(act == "Called (paid off)"), 1),
            `Gave up %` = percent(mean(act == "Checked / gave up"), 1), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(brt, align = "lrrrr", row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r busted-river-note, results='asis'}
bl <- filter(br, act == "Bet it (bluff)")
```
