```{r busted-river-note, results='asis'}
cat(sprintf('<p class="meta">Across the whole sample, betting a busted draw is roughly breakeven (%d bets, %s) - a balance / board-coverage play, not a money-printer. By this measure your bluffing is flat-to-down recently (%s vs %s of busted-draw rivers), so the adjustment is not showing up here yet. CAVEAT: this counts only busted-DRAW bluffs; pure-air bluffs (no draw) need full 7-card reconstruction and are not captured - treat it as a lower bound.</p>',
  nrow(bl), tt(sum(bl$net)), percent(bet_share("earlier"), 1), percent(bet_share("recent"), 1)))
```

### Bets by hand class: value, semi-bluff, air

Now that the postflop engine evaluates Hero's hand at every street, we can decompose **what backs each
bet**. A "bluff" here = a bet where your best five-card hand using a hole card is **no pair or better** -
so a paired *board* you don't share never counts as a hand. Within that, what equity is behind it: a
**draw** (flush / straight, with cards to come), **overcards**, or **pure air**? Made-hand bets are split
into **value** (two pair+) and **marginal** (one pair). River has no cards to come, so a missed hand is
either ace/over-high or air.

```{r bet-anatomy}
anat <- function(streetbet, made, fd, sdraw, overs, is_river) {
  has <- !is.na(streetbet) & streetbet > 0 & !is.na(made)
  cls <- rep(NA_character_, length(made))
  cls[has & made >= 2] <- "Value (2pair+)"
  cls[has & made == 1] <- "Marginal (one pair)"
  air <- has & made == 0
  if (is_river) {
    cls[air & overs >= 1] <- "Air - ace/over-high"
    cls[air & overs == 0] <- "Air - nothing"
  } else {
    cls[air & (fd | sdraw != "none")] <- "Semi-bluff (draw)"
    cls[air & !(fd | sdraw != "none") & overs >= 1] <- "Bluff - overcards"
    cls[air & !(fd | sdraw != "none") & overs == 0] <- "Bluff - pure air"
  }
  cls
}
cash$fl_bet_class <- anat(cash$hero_flop_bet,  cash$made_flop,  cash$fl_fd, cash$fl_sdraw, cash$fl_overs, FALSE)
cash$tn_bet_class <- anat(cash$hero_turn_bet,  cash$made_turn,  cash$tn_fd, cash$tn_sdraw, cash$tn_overs, FALSE)
cash$rv_bet_class <- anat(cash$hero_river_bet, cash$made_river, FALSE, "none",
                          ifelse(is.na(cash$made_river), 0, 0), TRUE)  # river overs handled in engine via river_backing
# river over-high: recover from river_backing where it's a bluff, else from made
cash$rv_bet_class[!is.na(cash$river_backing) & cash$river_backing == "ace/over-high"] <- "Air - ace/over-high"
cash$rv_bet_class[!is.na(cash$river_backing) & cash$river_backing == "air"]           <- "Air - nothing"

anat_tbl <- function(cls, betcol, potcol, lv) {
  d <- data.frame(cls = cls, net = cash$net, net_bb = cash$net_bb, betpot = cash[[betcol]] / cash[[potcol]])
  d <- d[!is.na(d$cls), ]
  d %>% group_by(`What's behind it` = factor(cls, lv)) %>%
    summarise(Bets = n(), `Median size (x pot)` = sprintf("%.2f", median(betpot, na.rm = TRUE)),
              Net = tt(sum(net)), `bb/100*` = sprintf("%+.0f", sum(net_bb) / n() * 100),
              .groups = "drop")
}
fl_lv <- c("Value (2pair+)", "Marginal (one pair)", "Semi-bluff (draw)", "Bluff - overcards", "Bluff - pure air")
rv_lv <- c("Value (2pair+)", "Marginal (one pair)", "Air - ace/over-high", "Air - nothing")
```

```{r bet-anatomy-flop}
knitr::kable(anat_tbl(cash$fl_bet_class, "hero_flop_bet", "hero_flop_pot", fl_lv),
             align = "lrrrr", caption = "Flop bets, by what's behind them")
```

```{r bet-anatomy-river}
knitr::kable(anat_tbl(cash$rv_bet_class, "hero_river_bet", "hero_river_pot", rv_lv),
             align = "lrrrr", caption = "River bets, by what's behind them")
```

> This splits aggression into value, one pair, draws and overcards (semi-bluffs, which are supposed to
> bet), and pure air. A large pure-air share would mean bluffing too much; a large semi-bluff share is
> normal aggression.
> *(\*Per-class bb/100 is a within-bucket rate, not comparable to the overall - outcome-selected.)*

### River bluffs by size over time

Has river bluff sizing changed over time? River bets with **no made hand** (ace-high / air), bucketed by size,
earlier vs recent:

```{r river-bluff-size}
rvb <- cash %>% filter(!is.na(river_bluff), river_bluff, !is.na(river_betpot)) %>%
  mutate(size = cut(river_betpot, c(0, 0.4, 0.7, Inf),
                    labels = c("small (<=1/3)", "medium (~1/2)", "big (>=2/3)")),
         era = ifelse(as.Date(dt) >= median(as.Date(cash$dt)), "recent", "earlier"))
if (nrow(rvb) >= 5) {
  rs <- rvb %>% group_by(`Bet size` = size) %>%
    summarise(Bets = n(), `Got called %` = percent(mean(showdown == 1), 1),
              Net = tt(sum(net)), .groups = "drop")
  knitr::kable(rs, align = "lrrr", row.names = FALSE)
} else cat(sprintf('<p class="meta">Only %d no-made-hand river bets in the sample - too few to bucket by size yet. </p>', nrow(rvb)))
```

```{r river-bluff-size-note, results='asis'}
if (nrow(rvb) >= 5) {
  byera <- rvb %>% group_by(era) %>% summarise(big = mean(size == "big (>=2/3)"), .groups = "drop")
  ge <- function(e) { v <- byera$big[byera$era == e]; if (length(v)) percent(v, 1) else "n/a" }
  cat(sprintf('<p class="meta">Share of your river bluff-bets that are big (>=2/3 pot): %s earlier vs %s recent. Small sample - treat as a signal, not proof.</p>', ge("earlier"), ge("recent")))
}
```

## C-bets by board texture

The flop's *texture* should change how you play: on **dry** boards the preflop raiser's range is
ahead, so c-bets print; on **wet** boards (flushy/connected) and **monotone** boards villains
connect more, so betting should slow down. This classifies every flop you saw and checks whether
your c-bet frequency and results actually move with the board. ("Wet" = monotone, or two-tone and
connected; "Dry" = rainbow and disconnected; "Paired" pulled out separately.)

```{r texture-calc}
flop_texture <- function(f) {
  c <- cardsplit(f); if (length(c) < 3) return(NA_character_)
  r <- crank(c); su <- csuit(c); paired <- any(duplicated(r))
  suit <- if (length(unique(su)) == 1) "mono" else if (length(unique(su)) == 2) "two-tone" else "rainbow"
  connected <- !paired && (max(r) - min(r)) <= 4
  if (paired) return("Paired")
  if (suit == "mono") return("Wet (monotone)")
  if (connected && suit == "two-tone") return("Wet (conn. + flushy)")
  if (connected || suit == "two-tone") return("Semi-wet")
  "Dry (rainbow)"
}
lev <- c("Dry (rainbow)", "Semi-wet", "Wet (conn. + flushy)", "Wet (monotone)", "Paired")
tx <- cash %>% filter(saw_flop, !is.na(flop))
tx$tex <- factor(vapply(tx$flop, flop_texture, character(1)), levels = lev)
```

```{r texture-table}
txt <- tx %>% group_by(`Flop texture` = tex) %>%
  summarise(Flops = n(), `C-bet %` = percent(sum(cbet_flop) / pmax(sum(cbet_opp), 1), 1),
            `Won when saw flop` = percent(mean(net > 0), 1),
            `bb/100` = sprintf("%+.0f", sum(net_bb) / n() * 100), Net = tt(sum(net)), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(txt, align = "lrrrrr")
```

```{r texture-chart, fig.height=3.4}
txc <- tx %>% group_by(tex) %>%
  summarise(cbet = sum(cbet_flop) / pmax(sum(cbet_opp), 1), n = sum(cbet_opp), .groups = "drop")
ggplot(txc, aes(tex, cbet, fill = tex == "Wet (monotone)")) +
  geom_col(width = 0.65) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.0f%% (n=%d)", cbet * 100, n)), vjust = -0.4, size = 3.3, color = ink) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = red, `FALSE` = green), guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent, limits = c(0, max(txc$cbet) * 1.15)) +
  labs(title = "Your flop c-bet % by texture (it should NOT be flat)", x = NULL, y = "c-bet %") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 15, hjust = 1))
```

> A good c-bet strategy leans on texture: more often on dry, unconnected boards, less on monotone and
> connected ones, carefully on paired boards where what beats one pair is two pair or better. A flat
> c-bet rate across textures is the thing to look for.

### Texture gap over time

The one number to move: **c-bet on dry rainbow *minus* c-bet on monotone**. If you're adjusting, dry
goes **up**, monotone goes **down**, and this **gap grows positive**. Split earlier vs recent (median-date)
so you can watch it shift as you add sessions — it re-computes every time you parse new hands.

```{r texture-adjust}
adj <- tx %>% filter(tex %in% c("Dry (rainbow)", "Wet (monotone)")) %>%
  mutate(era = ifelse(as.Date(dt) >= median(as.Date(cash$dt)), "recent", "earlier")) %>%
  group_by(tex, era) %>% summarise(cb = sum(cbet_flop) / pmax(sum(cbet_opp), 1), n = sum(cbet_opp), .groups = "drop")
cbof <- function(t, e) { v <- adj$cb[adj$tex == t & adj$era == e]; if (length(v)) v else NA_real_ }
nof  <- function(t, e) { v <- adj$n[adj$tex == t & adj$era == e]; if (length(v)) v else 0L }
at <- data.frame(
  Texture = c("Dry (rainbow): fire MORE", "Wet (monotone): fire LESS", "GAP (dry minus mono)"),
  Earlier = c(percent(cbof("Dry (rainbow)","earlier"),1), percent(cbof("Wet (monotone)","earlier"),1),
              percent(cbof("Dry (rainbow)","earlier") - cbof("Wet (monotone)","earlier"),1)),
  Recent  = c(percent(cbof("Dry (rainbow)","recent"),1),  percent(cbof("Wet (monotone)","recent"),1),
              percent(cbof("Dry (rainbow)","recent")  - cbof("Wet (monotone)","recent"),1)),
  `n (recent)` = c(nof("Dry (rainbow)","recent"), nof("Wet (monotone)","recent"), NA),
  check.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(at, align = "lrrr", row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r texture-adjust-note, results='asis'}
ge <- cbof("Dry (rainbow)","earlier") - cbof("Wet (monotone)","earlier")
gr <- cbof("Dry (rainbow)","recent")  - cbof("Wet (monotone)","recent")
dir <- if (is.na(gr - ge)) "not enough recent monotone flops to read yet" else
       if (gr > ge) sprintf("moving the right way (gap %s -> %s)", percent(ge,1), percent(gr,1)) else
       sprintf("not adjusting yet (gap %s -> %s)", percent(ge,1), percent(gr,1))
cat(sprintf('<p class="meta">Goal: a clearly <b>positive, growing</b> gap. Right now it&rsquo;s <b>%s</b>. Monotone flops are rare (recent n=%d), so the recent column needs a few sessions before it means much.</p>', dir, nof("Wet (monotone)","recent")))
```

## Betting lines

When do your bets actually fold people out, and do multi-street barrels work? This tracks every bet
you make on each street — its size relative to the pot, whether it took the pot down (everyone
folded), and the net — plus the full flop-turn-river *line* you took. (Single-board hands;
"folded out" = no one continued to the next street, or no showdown on the river.)

```{r lines-calc}
flopeq <- function(hc, fl) {
  he <- cardsplit(hc); bd <- cardsplit(fl)
  if (length(he) < 2 || length(bd) < 3) return(NA_character_)
  a <- c(he, bd)
  if (has_flush(a, he) || has_straight(a, he)) return("made hand")
  if (max(table(crank(a))) >= 2) return("made hand")
  if (draw_here(a, he)) return("draw")
  "air"
}
streetbets <- bind_rows(
  cash %>% filter(hero_flop_bet  > 0, hero_flop_pot  > 0) %>% transmute(street = "Flop",  bp = hero_flop_bet/hero_flop_pot,   fo = is.na(turn_card),  net),
  cash %>% filter(hero_turn_bet  > 0, hero_turn_pot  > 0) %>% transmute(street = "Turn",  bp = hero_turn_bet/hero_turn_pot,   fo = is.na(river_card), net),
  cash %>% filter(hero_river_bet > 0, hero_river_pot > 0) %>% transmute(street = "River", bp = hero_river_bet/hero_river_pot, fo = !showdown,          net)
) %>% mutate(street = factor(street, levels = c("Flop","Turn","River")),
             Size = cut(bp, c(0, 0.4, 0.7, Inf), labels = c("small (<=1/3)", "medium (~1/2)", "big (>=2/3)")))
bl <- cash %>% mutate(
  bf = hero_flop_bet > 0 & !is.na(hero_flop_bet),
  bt = hero_turn_bet > 0 & !is.na(hero_turn_bet),
  br = hero_river_bet > 0 & !is.na(hero_river_bet),
  line = paste0(ifelse(bf, "B", "-"), ifelse(bt, "B", "-"), ifelse(br, "B", "-")))
```

### Fold equity by street and size

```{r street-foldequity}
streetbets %>% group_by(Street = street, Size) %>%
  summarise(Bets = n(), `Folded out %` = percent(mean(fo), 1), Net = tt(sum(net)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  knitr::kable(align = "llrrr")
```

> Fold equity normally rises with bet size. If small bets fold few opponents, cheap bluffs aren't buying
> much against this pool, and the fold equity lives in the bigger sizes.

### Small c-bets by hand class

```{r flop-cbet-equity}
fb <- cash %>% filter(hero_flop_bet > 0, hero_flop_pot > 0, !is.na(flop), nchar(hero_cards) >= 4) %>%
  mutate(small = hero_flop_bet / hero_flop_pot <= 0.4, foldout = is.na(turn_card))
fb$eq <- mapply(flopeq, fb$hero_cards, fb$flop)
fb %>% filter(small, !is.na(eq)) %>% mutate(eq = factor(eq, levels = c("air", "draw", "made hand"))) %>%
  group_by(`Your flop equity` = eq) %>%
  summarise(`Small c-bets` = n(), `Folded out %` = percent(mean(foldout), 1),
            Net = tt(sum(net)), `Avg/bet` = tt(mean(net)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  knitr::kable(align = "lrrrr")
```

> Splitting small c-bets by hand class separates two different bets: thin value with a made hand,
> which profits when worse hands call, and cheap bluffs with air, which need folds. If the air version
> loses, check it or size up rather than firing small.

### Lines by street (flop-turn-river)

`B` = you bet that street, `-` = checked / didn't bet. So `B--` is a flop c-bet then give up, `-BB`
is check-flop then barrel turn and river.

```{r betting-lines}
bl %>% filter(bf | bt | br) %>% group_by(Line = line) %>%
  summarise(Hands = n(), Net = tt(sum(net)), `Avg/hand` = tt(mean(net)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(Hands)) %>% knitr::kable(align = "lrrr")
```

> Each line is a street-by-street sequence (B = bet, - = check or call). One- and two-street value
> lines normally carry the profit. A triple barrel (`BBB`) near break-even usually means thin value
> is getting called by better or bluffs aren't getting folds.

### Calls facing bets (flop and turn)

The defensive flip side: when a villain *bets* into you on the flop or turn, how do your calls do by
their size? (River calls are bucketed earlier; this is the earlier streets.) Bet sizes are the
villain's bet as a share of the pot.

```{r facing-calc}
facing <- bind_rows(
  cash %>% filter(flop_call > 0, !is.na(flop_call_pot), flop_call_pot > flop_call) %>%
    transmute(Street = "Flop", betpot = flop_call / (flop_call_pot - flop_call), net),
  cash %>% filter(turn_call > 0, !is.na(turn_call_pot), turn_call_pot > turn_call) %>%
    transmute(Street = "Turn", betpot = turn_call / (turn_call_pot - turn_call), net)
) %>% mutate(Street = factor(Street, levels = c("Flop", "Turn")),
             Size = cut(betpot, c(0, 0.5, 0.75, Inf), labels = c("< 1/2 pot", "1/2 - 3/4 pot", ">= 3/4 pot")))
```

```{r facing-table}
facing %>% group_by(Street, `Villain bet` = Size) %>%
  summarise(`Your calls` = n(), `Won %` = percent(mean(net > 0), 1), Net = tt(sum(net)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  knitr::kable(align = "llrrr")
```

> Small bets get called widely because they are cheap; that is where flop calls tend to lose, by peeling
> with weak hands and paying more on later streets. Compare the won share and net across sizes on each
> street: a size where calls lose consistently is the one to tighten against.

### Passive vs. aggressive lines

```{r passive-lines}
pa <- cash %>% filter(saw_flop) %>% mutate(
  bet_any = (hero_flop_bet > 0 & !is.na(hero_flop_bet)) | (hero_turn_bet > 0 & !is.na(hero_turn_bet)) | (hero_river_bet > 0 & !is.na(hero_river_bet)),
  called_any = flop_call > 0 | turn_call > 0 | river_call > 0,
  Line = ifelse(bet_any, "You bet >= 1 street", ifelse(called_any, "Check-call only (never bet)", "Checked down / folded")))
pa %>% group_by(`Postflop line` = Line) %>%
  summarise(Hands = n(), Net = tt(sum(net)), `Avg/hand` = tt(mean(net)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(Hands)) %>% knitr::kable(align = "lrrr")
```

> Betting at least one street nets **`r tt(sum(pa$net[pa$bet_any]))`**; check-call only nets
> **`r tt(sum(pa$net[!pa$bet_any & pa$called_any]))`**. Part of any gap is selection (strong hands get bet,
> marginal ones get called), so read the direction, not the size.

### Hand-trajectory clusters

The section above buckets hands by a literal bet/check string per street, chosen by us. This asks a
different question: if you hand k-means a richer feature set (preflop role, position, multiway,
bet-size-as-%-pot per street, call indicators, final made-hand strength, how far the hand went) and
let it group hands on its own, what comes out? This is genuinely **unsupervised** — cluster
membership never sees the hand's result — so it isn't limited by the hidden-information ceiling that
capped supervised prediction (a villain's hole cards, which supervised models tried to predict, are
never used here). **Caveats, upfront:** `k=6` and the feature list are modeling choices, not a
discovered truth; some described traits are correlated proxies for the same underlying fact (e.g.
"checks flop" and "calls flop" together just mean "passive on the flop," not two separate signals);
small clusters are noisier. Standalone + wired into every render (`hand_clusters.R`).

```{r hc-load}
hc <- tryCatch(read.csv("coinpoker_hand_clusters_summary.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE), error = function(e) NULL)
```

```{r hc-table, eval=!is.null(hc)}
ht <- hc %>% transmute(Cluster = cluster, Hands = n, `What it looks like` = Description,
                        Net = tt(Net), `bb/100` = sprintf("%+.0f", `bb.100`))
knitr::kable(ht, align = "clrrr", caption = "Hand-trajectory clusters, found by k-means (not hand-picked)")
```

```{r hc-chart, eval=!is.null(hc), fig.height=3.4}
hc$lab <- factor(sprintf("C%d", hc$cluster), levels = sprintf("C%d", hc$cluster[order(-hc$bb.100)]))
ggplot(hc, aes(reorder(lab, bb.100), bb.100, fill = bb.100 >= 0)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6) + coord_flip() + geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = ink) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = green, `FALSE` = red), guide = "none") +
  labs(title = "bb/100 by cluster", x = NULL, y = "bb/100")
```

```{r hc-note, results='asis', eval=!is.null(hc)}
best <- hc$Description[which.max(hc$bb.100)]; worst <- hc$Description[which.min(hc$bb.100)]
cat(sprintf('<p class="meta">The clusters are found from the shape of each hand (streets reached, who bet, pot size) without seeing any result. Best cluster by bb/100: <b>%s</b>; worst: <b>%s</b>. If they line up with the leak ledger and betting-lines sections, that is an independent cross-check, since this method never saw an outcome.</p>',
  best, worst))
```

```{r hc-missing, results='asis', eval=is.null(hc)}
cat('<p class="meta">No <code>coinpoker_hand_clusters_summary.csv</code> found &mdash; run <code>Rscript hand_clusters.R</code> (render does this automatically).</p>')
```

## Position & pot size

Two structural cuts: how many players you're up against (heads-up vs multiway), and whether you have
position (act last) or not. "OOP" here = you were first to act on the flop — exact heads-up, a strong
proxy multiway.

```{r pospot-calc}
sf <- cash %>% filter(saw_flop, !is.na(n_flop))
```

### Heads-up vs. multiway

```{r hu-mw}
sf %>% mutate(`Pot` = ifelse(n_flop <= 2, "Heads-up", "Multiway (3+)")) %>%
  group_by(Pot) %>%
  summarise(Flops = n(), `Won when saw flop` = percent(mean(net > 0), 1),
            `bb/100` = sprintf("%+.0f", sum(net_bb) / n() * 100), Net = tt(sum(net)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  knitr::kable(align = "lrrrr")
```

> Heads-up and multiway pots are different games: one pair and draws lose value fast as players are
> added, and thin value bets and bluffs work worse against several opponents. If multiway pots trail
> heads-up ones, the usual adjustment is to continue with stronger hands multiway.

### In position vs. out of position

```{r ip-oop}
sf %>% filter(!is.na(hero_first_flop)) %>%
  mutate(Position = ifelse(hero_first_flop, "OOP (act first)", "IP (act last)")) %>%
  group_by(Position) %>%
  summarise(Flops = n(), `Won when saw flop` = percent(mean(net > 0), 1),
            `Went to showdown` = percent(mean(showdown), 1),
            `bb/100` = sprintf("%+.0f", sum(net_bb) / n() * 100), Net = tt(sum(net)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  knitr::kable(align = "lrrrrr")
```

```{r ip-oop-potsize}
sf %>% filter(!is.na(hero_first_flop)) %>%
  mutate(Position = ifelse(hero_first_flop, "OOP", "IP"), Pot = ifelse(n_flop <= 2, "Heads-up", "Multiway")) %>%
  group_by(Position, Pot) %>% summarise(Flops = n(), Net = tt(sum(net)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  knitr::kable(align = "llrr")
```

> An aggregate by position mixes two very different situations, raising preflop and calling preflop.
> The breakdown below separates them.

#### Position split by preflop role

Splitting each by whether you were the preflop **aggressor** (you raised) or a **caller**:

```{r ip-oop-2x2}
sf %>% filter(!is.na(hero_first_flop)) %>%
  mutate(Position = ifelse(hero_first_flop, "OOP", "IP"),
         Role = ifelse(hero_pf_aggr, "Aggressor (raised pre)", "Caller (called pre)")) %>%
  group_by(Position, Role) %>%
  summarise(Flops = n(), `bb/100` = sprintf("%+.0f", sum(net_bb) / n() * 100), Net = tt(sum(net)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  knitr::kable(align = "llrr")
```

> This splits each side by who raised preflop. In-position play as the preflop raiser should be the
> best spot; in-position play as a caller is where passive players lose, by peeling and calling down
> instead of betting when checked to. If the two in-position rows point in opposite directions, the
> average above hides the real problem: what's done with position, not position itself.

#### C-bet fold rate in and out of position

How often a flop c-bet takes the pot right away, in position and out of position:

```{r ip-oop-cbet-fe}
sf %>% filter(cbet_flop == 1, !is.na(hero_first_flop)) %>%
  mutate(pos = ifelse(hero_first_flop, "OOP c-bet", "IP c-bet"), foldout = is.na(turn_card)) %>%
  group_by(`Your c-bet` = pos) %>%
  summarise(`C-bets` = n(), `Folded everyone out %` = percent(mean(foldout), 1), Net = tt(sum(net)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  knitr::kable(align = "lrrr")
```

> C-bets normally fold more opponents in position. If they do here, the in-position calling hands above
> are missing the spots where betting works best: when checked to in position, bet more and call less.

## Leak ledger

Every leak this dashboard found, tagged per hand and summed. **Two views, on purpose.** Each leak is a
*hypothesis* associated with lost chips, not a proven cause of any one hand — and a single hand can carry
several tags at once, so you can't just add them up. So: **(1) the independent view** measures each leak's
size on its own (these overlap and intentionally *don't* sum to your net); **(2) the attribution view**
gives every *losing* hand its single most-proximal leak, so those buckets sum cleanly and answer "what is
my loss actually made of?"

```{r ledger-calc}
# NOTE: lk_light_3bet is intentionally excluded - on this sample the corrected (genuinely
# light, vs early openers only) version is ~breakeven, so it is not a leak. See note below.
leakdefs <- c(lk_busted_sd = "Busted draw taken to showdown", lk_paid_river = "Paid off river with a weak hand",
              lk_loose_passive = "Loose & passive in position",
              lk_loose_entry = "Loose entry (range too wide)", lk_air_bet = "Bet (near-)air postflop",
              lk_skipped_steal = "Skipped steal (range too tight)")
ind <- bind_rows(lapply(names(leakdefs), function(k) {
  sel <- !is.na(cash[[k]]) & cash[[k]]
  data.frame(key = k, Leak = unname(leakdefs[k]), Hands = sum(sel),
             net = sum(cash$net[sel]), net_bb = sum(cash$net_bb[sel]), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
})) %>% arrange(net)

# primary attribution: each losing hand -> one dominant leak (engine column)
prilab <- c(paid_river = "Paid off river with a weak hand", busted_sd = "Busted draw taken to showdown",
            loose_passive = "Loose & passive in position",
            loose_entry = "Loose entry (range too wide)")
pa <- cash %>% filter(!is.na(primary_leak)) %>% group_by(primary_leak) %>%
  summarise(Hands = n(), net = sum(net), .groups = "drop") %>% arrange(net)
pa$Leak <- unname(prilab[pa$primary_leak])
pa_attr <- sum(pa$net)
loss_total <- sum(cash$net[cash$net < 0])
```

### View 1: each leak on its own (overlapping)

```{r ledger-independent}
it <- ind %>% transmute(Leak, Hands, Net = tt(net),
                        `bb/100*` = sprintf("%+.0f", net_bb / pmax(Hands, 1) * 100))
knitr::kable(it, align = "lrrr", row.names = FALSE)
```

<p class="meta">Overlapping by design (one hand can be several leaks) - the Net column does **not** sum to
your result. "Skipped steal" shows positive because those are *folds* (saved blinds / opportunity cost),
not realized losses; it rides in the independent view but is excluded from the attribution waterfall below.
*Per-leak bb/100 is a within-bucket rate, not comparable to your overall.*</p>

### View 2: losses attributed to leaks

Each **losing** hand assigned its single most-proximal leak (river call > busted draw to showdown > loose
& passive > loose entry). These sum to a real number: `r tt(pa_attr)` across `r sum(pa$Hands)`
hands, which is `r percent(pa_attr/loss_total, 1)` of your total losing-hand volume (`r tt(loss_total)`).
The rest is untagged variance - losses we have **no named leak for** (coolers, run-bad, marginal spots).

```{r ledger-pareto}
pp <- pa %>% mutate(mag = -net) %>% arrange(desc(mag))
pp$cum <- cumsum(pp$mag) / sum(pp$mag)
short_lab <- c(paid_river = "River calls", busted_sd = "Busted draws", loose_passive = "Passive IP", loose_entry = "Loose entry")
pp$idx <- seq_len(nrow(pp)); pp$short <- unname(short_lab[pp$primary_leak])
plot_ly(pp, x = ~idx, height = 360) %>%
  add_bars(y = ~mag, name = "Loss attributed", marker = list(color = "#a8432f"),
           text = ~short, hovertemplate = "%{text}<br>%{y:.0f} T attributed<extra></extra>") %>%
  add_trace(y = ~cum, name = "Cumulative share", yaxis = "y2", type = "scatter", mode = "lines+markers",
            line = list(color = ink, width = 2), marker = list(color = ink, size = 5),
            hovertemplate = "%{y:.0%} of attributed loss<extra></extra>") %>%
  layout(title = list(text = "Leak Pareto: where the attributed losses concentrate",
                      font = list(size = 14, color = ink), x = 0.02),
         xaxis = list(title = "", tickmode = "array", tickvals = pp$idx, ticktext = pp$short, tickfont = list(size = 11)),
         yaxis = list(title = "T attributed"),
         yaxis2 = list(title = "Cumulative", overlaying = "y", side = "right", showgrid = FALSE,
                       range = c(0, 1.02), tickformat = ".0%"),
         legend = list(orientation = "h", x = 0, y = 1.12), hovermode = "x unified",
         margin = list(r = 62, t = 54))
```

### Leaks over time

A cumulative-cost line only ever slopes **down**, which makes "is this flattening out?" almost impossible to
read by eye. So instead of the running total, this shows each leak's **cost per 100 hands** over a **trailing
600-hand window** — roughly "how much is this leak bleeding me *right now*." The x-axis is cumulative hands
(a calendar axis would squeeze busy weeks and stretch quiet ones).
Read it off the **zero line**: a line sitting **at zero** means that leak has stopped accruing (leveled off);
a line **diving below zero** means it's actively costing you, and the deeper it goes the worse it's getting.
Per-leak totals are in View 2 above; this is purely the *trend*.

```{r ledger-time}
top_leaks <- pp$primary_leak[1:min(4, nrow(pp))]
ord <- cash %>% arrange(dt) %>% mutate(idx = row_number())
N <- nrow(ord); W <- 600
lo <- pmax(seq_len(N) - W, 0); win <- seq_len(N) - lo                 # trailing window (partial at the start)
roll100 <- function(v) { cs <- c(0, cumsum(v)); (cs[seq_len(N) + 1] - cs[lo + 1]) / win * 100 }
lcol <- c(paid_river = red, busted_sd = "#b98a3e", loose_passive = green, loose_entry = "#9aa7b0")
p <- plot_ly(height = 380)
for (k in top_leaks) {
  rate <- roll100(ifelse(ord$primary_leak %in% k, ord$net, 0))
  p <- add_trace(p, x = ord$idx, y = rate, name = unname(prilab[k]),
                 type = "scatter", mode = "lines", line = list(color = unname(lcol[k]), width = 2),
                 text = format(as.Date(ord$dt), "%b %d"),
                 hovertemplate = "%{text}<br>%{x} hands<br>%{y:.1f} T per 100 hands<extra></extra>")
}
p %>% layout(title = list(text = "Cost per 100 hands by leak (trailing 600-hand window)", font = list(size = 14, color = ink), x = 0.02),
             xaxis = list(title = "Cumulative hands played", tickfont = list(size = 10)),
             yaxis = list(title = "T per 100 hands (0 = not costing you now)", zeroline = TRUE,
                          zerolinecolor = "#5b6770", zerolinewidth = 1.5),
             legend = list(orientation = "h", x = 0, y = 1.14), hovermode = "x unified", margin = list(t = 60))
```

> Read the ledger top-down. Two numbers matter for each leak: the total it cost and how concentrated
> it is (cost per hand). A concentrated leak (large losses in few hands) is usually one decision to
> change; a diffuse one (many small losses) is a habit, slower to fix. River pay-offs and busted draws
> taken to showdown are the same root decision, calling a river when beaten, so read them as one.

## Counterfactual replay with simple rules

Re-runs your actual hand history under four mechanical policies and compares the alternate
bankroll curve to what really happened. **Policies A/B (fold loose hands) are clean counterfactuals**
— each hand's result is swapped independently using only the range model's own classification, with
the blind you'd still post priced in (folding the SB isn't free). **Policies C/D (session hand-cap,
stop-loss) are hindsight, not a proven real-time rule** — an unplayed hand nets exactly $0, so the
arithmetic is exact, but this can't tell you whether you'd have known to quit *before* seeing the
result. Standalone + wired into every render (`counterfactual_replay.R`).

```{r cf-load}
cf <- tryCatch(read.csv("coinpoker_counterfactual.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE), error = function(e) NULL)
cf_curves <- tryCatch(read.csv("coinpoker_counterfactual_curves.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE), error = function(e) NULL)
cf_ok <- !is.null(cf) && !is.null(cf_curves)
```

```{r cf-table, eval=cf_ok}
ct <- cf %>% transmute(Policy = policy, Net = tt(net), `bb/100` = sprintf("%+.1f", bb100),
                        `vs. actual` = tt(delta_vs_actual))
knitr::kable(ct, align = "lrrr", caption = "Counterfactual replay: net result under each policy")
```

```{r cf-chart, eval=cf_ok, fig.height=4}
pol_cols <- c(actual = ink, A = "#9aa7b0", B = "#c4ccd1", C = green, D = "#7fa8cf")
pol_lab <- c(actual = "Actual", A = "A: fold loose SB", B = "B: fold all loose",
             C = "C: session hand-cap", D = "D: stop-loss 3 buy-ins")
p <- plot_ly(height = 380)
for (k in names(pol_lab))
  p <- add_trace(p, data = cf_curves, x = ~idx, y = as.formula(paste0("~", k)), name = pol_lab[[k]],
                  type = "scatter", mode = "lines",
                  line = list(color = pol_cols[[k]], width = ifelse(k == "actual", 2.2, 1.4),
                              dash = ifelse(k == "actual", "solid", "dot")))
p %>% layout(title = list(text = "Cumulative bb: actual vs. each policy", font = list(size = 14)),
             xaxis = list(title = "hands played", gridcolor = grid),
             yaxis = list(title = "cumulative bb", gridcolor = grid, zeroline = TRUE, zerolinecolor = ink),
             legend = list(orientation = "h", y = -0.2), margin = list(t = 40)) %>%
  config(displaylogo = FALSE, modeBarButtonsToRemove = c("select2d", "lasso2d", "autoScale2d"))
```

```{r cf-note, results='asis', eval=cf_ok}
a_delta <- cf$delta_vs_actual[cf$policy == "A: fold loose SB hands"]
c_delta <- cf$delta_vs_actual[grepl("^C:", cf$policy)]
d_delta <- cf$delta_vs_actual[grepl("^D:", cf$policy)]
cat(sprintf('<p class="meta">Folding loose small-blind hands would have made the result %s by %s. Policy C (a flat cap on hands per session) changes it by %s; policy D (stopping after a set loss) by %s. If C recovers more than D, playing less per session matters more than quitting when stuck. These are replays of the same hands with simple rules, not predictions.</p>',
  ifelse(a_delta < 0, "worse", "better"), tt(abs(a_delta)), tt(c_delta), tt(d_delta)))
```

## Value attribution by decision

The leak ledger above is **result** attribution: it sorts hands by how they *finished*. This section is
**value** attribution — it asks whether a decision was correctly priced **at the moment you made it**,
before the board decided anything. A call can be perfectly +EV and still lose; a thin one can win and still
have been a mistake. We can score two decision types objectively from the price and your equity alone, with
no read on the villain required. *(The most recent day is held out as a test set; these descriptive tables
use all hands.)*

### Break-even fold rates for bluffs and semi-bluffs

For a bet with no made hand, the objective number is the **breakeven fold %**: how often the villain has to
fold for the bet to profit. Pure air needs `bet / (bet + pot)`; a semi-bluff needs **less**, because the
draw wins some of the times you get called.

```{r va-bets}
bt <- dec %>% filter(decision %in% c("bluff_bet", "semibluff_bet"))
btt <- bt %>%
  group_by(Street = factor(street, c("flop", "turn", "river")),
           Type = ifelse(decision == "semibluff_bet", "semi-bluff (has a draw)", "bluff (no equity)")) %>%
  summarise(Bets = n(),
            `Median fold% needed` = percent(median(breakeven_fold), 1),
            `Cheap (<40% needed)` = sprintf("%d", sum(breakeven_fold < 0.40)),
            `Need >55%` = sprintf("%d", sum(breakeven_fold > 0.55)), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(btt, align = "llrrrr", row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Bluff/semi-bluff bets, by the fold % required to break even")
```

> The lower the break-even fold rate, the cheaper the bet. A median under about 40% means most bets
> only need ordinary folding to profit; many bets above 55% would mean the bluffs are priced too high.
> This is the conservative read: semi-bluffs can also improve or barrel later, which lowers the real bar.

### Implied odds needed for draw calls

Draws are harder, and the honest framing took a revision. A first instinct was to **bracket** each call
between rule-of-2 (one card) and rule-of-4 (both cards) odds — but rule-of-4 is *not* an upper bound: a
draw's **implied odds** (the extra you win when it gets there) sit *above* it, so "−EV even at rule-of-4"
wouldn't actually mean "mistake." So we drop the bracket. The clean, assumption-free quantity is the
**implied-odds breakeven**: taking the immediate price and one-card equity as given, how much *more* must
you win when you hit to make the call break even —

$$X = \frac{(1-e)\,C}{e} - P \qquad\text{(extra to win on later streets, expressed below as a multiple of the call }C\text{).}$$

A call that's already +EV on the immediate price needs **none** ("priced now"). Everything else needs
implied odds — and then the question is whether you actually *collect* them, which we can measure.

```{r va-draws}
dr  <- dec %>% filter(decision == "draw_call")
drh <- dr %>% distinct(id, .keep_all = TRUE)   # hand-level for realized $ (a hand can hold flop AND turn draw calls)
drt <- dr %>% group_by(Street = factor(street, c("flop", "turn"))) %>%
  summarise(`Draw calls` = n(),
            `Priced now` = percent(mean(good), 1),
            `Implied odds needed` = sprintf("%.1fx call", median(req_implied_x[!good])),
            `Predicted hit` = percent(mean(equity), 1),
            `Realized hit` = percent(mean(hit), 1), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(drt, align = "lrrrrr", row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Draw calls: the implied-odds bar, and whether the draw actually hit")
```

```{r va-draws-hist}
dn <- dr %>% filter(!good, req_implied_x > 0, req_implied_x < 12)
plot_ly(dn, x = ~req_implied_x, type = "histogram", height = 320,
        marker = list(color = "#b98a3e", line = list(color = "white", width = 1)),
        hovertemplate = "need %{x:.1f}x the call<br>%{y} draw calls<extra></extra>") %>%
  layout(title = list(text = "How steep is the implied-odds bar on your draw calls?",
                      font = list(size = 14, color = ink), x = 0.02),
         xaxis = list(title = "extra winnings needed when you hit (x the call)"),
         yaxis = list(title = "draw calls"), bargap = 0.05, margin = list(t = 50))
```

```{r va-draws-note, results='asis'}
won <- drh$net[drh$hit]; brk <- drh$net[!drh$hit]
cat(sprintf('<p class="meta"><b>The calibration is the punchline.</b> Your draws hit %s of the time against a predicted %s &mdash; the evaluator&rsquo;s out-counts are honest, not optimistic. But when they hit you netted only %s on average, against misses of %s, so the whole draw-calling group nets <b>%s</b> over %d hands. Translation: most of these calls need %s the call back in implied odds, and you&rsquo;re not collecting it. The fix isn&rsquo;t to stop drawing &mdash; it&rsquo;s to draw on the calls that are <i>priced now</i> or close, and fold the thin ones that need a big future payoff you rarely get (the right tail of the chart above).</p>',
  percent(mean(drh$hit), 1), percent(mean(dr$equity), 1), tt(mean(won)), tt(mean(brk)),
  tt(sum(drh$net)), nrow(drh), sprintf("%.1fx", median(dr$req_implied_x[!dr$good]))))
```

## Missed betting opportunities

Value attribution scores the decisions you *did* make. This flips it: where did you reach a street with a
bet available and **check** instead? Two kinds — **missed value** (a made hand checked down that a worse
hand would have paid) and **missed bluffs** (air/busted draws given up in spots where the pool folds). The
`$` figures are **rough, pool-calibrated estimates for ranking only** (villains fold ~60% / call ~40% on
rivers, measured from these same histories) — they sort the spots, they don't claim precise EV. Full list
in `coinpoker_missed_ops.csv`.

```{r mo-load}
mo <- tryCatch(read.csv("coinpoker_missed_ops.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
               error = function(e) NULL)
mo_lab <- c(missed_value_strong = "Checked a strong made hand (2 pair+) that won",
            missed_value_thin   = "Checked a winning one pair (thin value)",
            turn_monster_checked= "Slow-played a set+ on the turn",
            small_value_river   = "Bet a big hand too small (<40% pot)",
            missed_bluff_busted = "Gave up a busted draw (no bluff)",
            missed_bluff_air    = "Gave up air with fold equity")
```

```{r mo-summary, eval=!is.null(mo) && nrow(mo) > 0}
sm <- mo %>%
  mutate(What = factor(mo_lab[type], levels = unname(mo_lab))) %>%
  group_by(What) %>%
  summarise(Spots = n(), `Est. value left` = tt(sum(est_ev)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9.-]", "", `Est. value left`))))
knitr::kable(sm, align = "lrr", row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Where you left money by checking — ranked by rough estimated value")
```

```{r mo-note, results='asis', eval=!is.null(mo) && nrow(mo) > 0}
val <- sum(mo$est_ev[grepl("value|monster", mo$type)])
blf <- sum(mo$est_ev[grepl("bluff", mo$type)])
cat(sprintf('<p class="meta"><b>The surprise: your bigger river leak is missed <i>value</i>, not missed bluffs.</b> Checked-down made hands account for ~%s of estimated lost value across %d spots, versus only ~%s of missed bluffs (%d spots). You check sets, two pair, even full houses to showdown. When you <i>do</i> bet the river it prints &mdash; you simply don&rsquo;t bet enough, with either your strong hands or your busted ones. Same passivity root, quantified from the other side. <i>(Value estimate is an upper bound &mdash; some checks are defensible on wet boards; the bluff figure is conservative, so the value&gt;bluff direction is the trustworthy part.)</i></p>',
  tt(val), sum(grepl("value|monster", mo$type)), tt(blf), sum(grepl("bluff", mo$type))))
```

```{r mo-top, eval=!is.null(mo) && nrow(mo) > 0}
top <- mo %>% arrange(desc(est_ev)) %>% head(15) %>%
  transmute(Hand = hero_cards,
            Board = paste(flop, turn_card, river_card),
            Line = line, Spot = board,
            What = mo_lab[type], `~$` = tt(est_ev), Date = substr(dt, 1, 10))
knitr::kable(top, align = "lllllrr", row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Top 15 spots to replay (highest estimated value left)")
```

```{r mo-missing, results='asis', eval=is.null(mo) || nrow(mo) == 0}
cat('<p class="meta">No <code>coinpoker_missed_ops.csv</code> found &mdash; run <code>Rscript missed_ops.R</code> (render does this automatically).</p>')
```

## Scorecard against benchmark ranges

One place to see every key tendency against the band a winning 6-max reg lives in. "Read" just
says where you sit relative to that band — **direction of "good" depends on the stat** (e.g. a
lower fold-to-c-bet means you're stickier, not automatically better). Treat the small-denominator
rows (3-bet, fold-to-3-bet) as directional until they fill in.

```{r scorecard}
pf  <- function(x) percent(x, 0.1)
vp  <- mean(cash$vpip); pr <- mean(cash$pfr); gap <- vp - pr
tb  <- sum(cash$three_bet)    / pmax(sum(cash$vsopen_opp), 1)
f3  <- sum(cash$fold_to_3bet)  / pmax(sum(cash$ftb_opp),    1)
cb  <- sum(cash$cbet_flop)     / pmax(sum(cash$cbet_opp),   1)
fcb <- sum(cash$fold_to_cbet)  / pmax(sum(cash$fcbet_opp),  1)
af  <- sum(cash$pf_aggr)       / pmax(sum(cash$pf_calls),   1)
wtsd <- mean(cash$showdown[cash$saw_flop]); wsd <- mean(cash$net[cash$showdown] > 0)
band <- function(x, lo, hi) ifelse(x < lo, "below band", ifelse(x > hi, "above band", "in band"))

sc <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Stat,           ~You,                       ~`Solid reg`, ~Read,
  "VPIP",          pf(vp),                     "22-27%",     band(vp,  .22, .27),
  "PFR",           pf(pr),                     "18-22%",     band(pr,  .18, .22),
  "VPIP-PFR gap",  sprintf("%.1f pts", gap*100), "5-8 pts",  band(gap, .05, .08),
  "3-bet",         pf(tb),                     "7-9%",       band(tb,  .07, .09),
  "Fold to 3-bet", pf(f3),                     "40-55%",     band(f3,  .40, .55),
  "C-bet flop",    pf(cb),                     "50-65%",     band(cb,  .50, .65),
  "Fold to c-bet", pf(fcb),                    "45-55%",     band(fcb, .45, .55),
  "Postflop AF",   sprintf("%.2f", af),        "2.0-3.0",    band(af,  2.0, 3.0),
  "WTSD",          pf(wtsd),                   "24-28%",     band(wtsd,.24, .28),
  "W$SD",          pf(wsd),                    "48-54%",     band(wsd, .48, .54))
knitr::kable(sc, align = "lrcl")
```

> Read these together rather than one at a time. A wide VPIP-PFR gap, a high WTSD with a low W$SD and a
> low postflop AF all point toward loose-passive play: calling too much preflop and calling down instead
> of betting. The opposite pattern (tight preflop, high AF, low WTSD) points toward over-folding.

## Rake & rakeback

You generated **`r tt(tot_fees)`** in fees — **`r tt(tot_rake)`** rake plus **`r tt(tot_splash)`**
in *splash fees* (a smaller house drop on nearly every pot, easy to overlook) — about
**`r sprintf("%.1f", sum(h$fees/h$bb)/n_hands*100)` bb/100**. These are *contribution-weighted*
(your share of each pot's drop), not whole-pot rake, so they reflect what you actually paid — and
they're the presumed basis CoinPoker's rakeback pays against.

```{r rake-by-stake}
cash %>% group_by(Stake = stake) %>%
  summarise(Hands = n(), Rake = tt(sum(hero_rake)), Splash = tt(sum(hero_splash)),
            `Fees bb/100` = sprintf("%.1f", sum(fees / bb) / n() * 100),
            `bb/100 before fees` = sprintf("%+.1f", sum((net + fees) / bb) / n() * 100),
            `bb/100 after fees` = sprintf("%+.1f", sum(net_bb)/n()*100), .groups = "drop") %>%
  knitr::kable(align = "lrrrrrr")
```

<p class="meta">Net per hand = collected − invested (top-offs/all-ins included), verified against stack
deltas. Position from the button; blinds identified from posts. bb/100 normalizes by each hand's
big blind.</p>

### Rakeback, from the claim ledger

Rakeback is claimed in lumps at irregular intervals. `rakeback_allocate.R` turns the claim ledger
(`coinpoker_rakeback.csv`) into per-hand and per-stake numbers. Both wired into every render. DATA_DICTIONARY §16 has
the full method and its caveats — the short version: **the total is exact** (real dollars you
actually received), the **stake-level split is modeled** (an aggregate rate applied to each hand's
own contributed fees, because the per-window implied rate is too noisy hand-claim to hand-claim to
trust directly — that instability is shown, not hidden, below).

```{r rb-load}
rb_ledger <- tryCatch(read.csv("coinpoker_rakeback.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE), error = function(e) NULL)
rb_stake <- tryCatch(read.csv("coinpoker_rakeback_by_stake.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE), error = function(e) NULL)
rb_overall <- tryCatch(read.csv("coinpoker_rakeback_overall.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE), error = function(e) NULL)
rb_windows <- tryCatch(read.csv("coinpoker_rakeback_windows.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE), error = function(e) NULL)
rb_ok <- !is.null(rb_ledger) && !is.null(rb_stake) && !is.null(rb_overall)
```

```{r rb-kpi, results='asis', eval=rb_ok}
cat(sprintf('<div class="kpi-row"><div class="kpi"><div class="kpi-label">Rakeback claimed</div><div class="kpi-value pos">%s</div><div class="kpi-sub">%d claims, %s &ndash; %s</div></div><div class="kpi"><div class="kpi-label">Net before &rarr; after</div><div class="kpi-value">%s &rarr; <span class="pos">%s</span></div><div class="kpi-sub">%+.1f &rarr; %+.1f bb/100</div></div><div class="kpi"><div class="kpi-label">Estimated still unclaimed</div><div class="kpi-value">%s</div><div class="kpi-sub">since your last claim, projected at the aggregate rate</div></div></div>',
  tt(rb_overall$rakeback), nrow(rb_ledger), substr(min(rb_ledger$dt), 1, 10), substr(max(rb_ledger$dt), 1, 10),
  tt(rb_overall$net_before), tt(rb_overall$net_after), rb_overall$bb100_before, rb_overall$bb100_after,
  tt(rb_overall$unclaimed_est)))
```

```{r rb-by-stake, eval=rb_ok}
rb_stake %>% transmute(Stake = stake, Hands = hands, Fees = tt(fees), Rakeback = tt(rakeback),
  `Net before` = tt(net_before), `Net after` = tt(net_after),
  `bb/100 before` = sprintf("%+.1f", bb100_before), `bb/100 after` = sprintf("%+.1f", bb100_after)) %>%
  knitr::kable(align = "lrrrrrrr", caption = "Rakeback allocated by stake (modeled split, exact overall total)")
```

```{r rb-window-note, results='asis', eval=rb_ok && !is.null(rb_windows)}
ir <- rb_windows$implied_rate[!is.na(rb_windows$implied_rate)]
cat(sprintf('<p class="meta">Why a flat rate: the per-claim implied rate (claim $ &divide; fees generated since the previous claim) ranges from %.0f%% to %.0f%% across the %d windows &mdash; some windows have almost no fee volume, which makes their individual ratio meaningless. The aggregate rate (total claimed &divide; total fees across the whole claimed period) is far more stable and is what&rsquo;s used above; it still conserves the real total exactly, only the stake-by-stake split is estimated.</p>',
  100 * min(ir), 100 * max(ir), nrow(rb_windows)))
```

```{r rb-missing, results='asis', eval=!rb_ok}
cat('<p class="meta">No rakeback claim ledger found (<code>coinpoker_rakeback.csv</code>). <code>simulate_hands.py</code> writes a synthetic one.</p>')
```

# Methods & scope — what this analysis measures

A map of the whole investigation: which streets, whose data, and what was measured, so the reads
above are easy to place. Everything is parsed straight from the raw CoinPoker hand histories.

### Data & trust
- **`r comma(nrow(h))` hands**, `r format(min(as.Date(h$dt)), "%b %d")`–`r format(max(as.Date(h$dt)), "%b %d, %Y")`, mostly 6-max. Duplicate hands across overlapping exports are removed by hand id.
- **Net** is rebuilt from Hero's own chips in/out and **reconciled to the next-hand stack delta**; mismatches are cash-outs/table-switches, not errors.
- **Pot** is reconstructed action by action and checked against the hand-history total (`pot_unaccounted` in the parsed table); that check is what makes the pot-relative sizing trustworthy.
- **Caveats**: postflop/showdown samples are small (read as *signals*, not proof); card-by-card analysis (draws, texture, sizing) uses **single-board hands** (run-it-twice excluded); win rates are **not yet statistically significant** at any stake; fees are **contribution-weighted** (your share of each pot's rake + splash).

### By street
- **Preflop** — VPIP, PFR, the VPIP–PFR gap, 3-bet, fold-to-3-bet, open-raise, all **by position**; starting-hand grid and card-luck.
- **Flop** — c-bet and fold-to-c-bet (overall, by position, **by board texture**); the street funnel (how often you continue).
- **Turn & river** — calls and call sizes, your own bets and bet sizes, showdown made-hands and what beat you.

### Your data (Hero)
Tendencies (VPIP/PFR/aggression/positional), starting-hand selection and P&L, postflop aggression
(c-bet, AF, WWSF), made hands at showdown, **draws** (flush/straight, hit vs miss), **set-mining**,
**river bet sizing** and the value/bluff mix behind it, and **recent form** (rolling, to catch course-corrections).

### Opponent data (villains)
Reconstructed from showdowns where they tabled a hand: **what beats you** (rank distribution of the
hands you lose to) and **river sizing tells** — reading their bet size against the hand they showed,
i.e. playing the hand backwards.

### Ranges & hands
The 13×13 starting-hand grid (your playing range), **card luck** (dealt vs combinatorially-expected
frequencies, with a chi-square check), hand-group and specific-hand P&L, and the made-hand
distribution at showdown.

### Bluff vs. value
Made-hand strength at showdown (yours and villains'), **busted draws taken to showdown**, and your
**river bets split into value / one-pair / bluff** by size.

### Sizing
**Villain** river bets bucketed by share of pot vs. the hand they showed; **your** river calls
bucketed pot-relative (where over-calling lives), and **your** river bets bucketed by size with
fold-out rate, net, and the value/bluff mix behind each size.
